items.title: A finite saddle omega-graph is strongly connected and is a finite union of polycycles
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a characteristic disk in the relative generic position of [[lem-characteristic-disk-map-can-be-put-in-generic-position-rel-boundary]]. Let $X$ be its planar characteristic vector field. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be an open neighborhood of the disk, and let $Y:U\to\mathbb R^2$ be a $C^1$ field with $Y=X$ and $DY=DX$ on $\Gamma$. Assume the positive orbit of $y$ has compact closure $K_0\Subset U$, $\Gamma=\omega_Y^+(y)$ contains at least one equilibrium, all equilibria in $\Gamma$ are nondegenerate characteristic saddles of $X$, and $\Gamma$ separates two specified points of the plane. Then $\Gamma$ is a finite embedded directed multigraph: its vertices are those saddles and its edges are closures of distinct nonconstant trajectories with saddle alpha- and omega-limits. The directed graph is strongly connected. Consequently every edge lies in a closed directed edge walk, and finitely many such walks cover $\Gamma$; a closed directed edge walk is allowed to repeat vertices and is called a directed saddle polycycle here.
items.strategy:
By [[lem-local-generalized-poincare-bendixson-for-a-precompact-planar-orbit]], every regular point of $\Gamma$ lies on a nonconstant trajectory with alpha- and omega-limits among the finite equilibrium set. The characteristic transverse function at a generic saddle has a nondegenerate Hessian of signature $(1,1)$; [[lem-c2-saddle-function-has-c1-morse-coordinates]] supplies C¹ coordinates $(x,y)$ with $u=xy$. The pulled-back source area form is $\mu=m(x,y)\,dx\wedge dy$ with $m$ continuous and positive, and $\beta=a(h)du$ with $a(h)$ continuous and nonzero. Thus $X=(a(h)/m)(x\partial_x-y\partial_y)$. The sign of $a(h)/m$ is constant on a smaller connected chart; if necessary interchange the stable and unstable axes. The zero-level axes are exactly two incoming and two outgoing half-branches. On each, $r=|x|$ or $|y|$ obeys $\dot r=\pm |a(h)/m|r$; continuity and nonvanishing give positive lower and finite upper rate bounds on a compact smaller chart, hence the exponential contraction/expansion estimates used below. Since $Y=X$ on $\Gamma$, every edge in $\Gamma$ follows one of those branches. Uniqueness makes each branch one global trajectory, so at most two edges leave each vertex and there are at most twice as many edges as vertices. Every regular point belongs to one of these trajectories, so their closures give exactly $\Gamma$. Distinct edges meet only at common saddle endpoints by uniqueness, and the four local sectors give the embedded graph structure.

The omega-limit set is internally chain-transitive, with exact endpoints. Fix $p,q\in\Gamma$, $\epsilon>0$ and $T>0$. By uniform continuity of the flow for times in $[T,2T]$ on a compact neighborhood of $\Gamma$, choose $\delta>0$ so $\delta$-close starting points have $\epsilon/3$-close images throughout that time interval. Since $p\in\omega_Y^+(y)$, choose a sufficiently late time $s$ with $Y_s(y)$ within $\delta$ of $p$. Since $q\in\omega_Y^+(y)$, choose a later time $t>s+2T$ with $Y_t(y)$ within $\delta$ of $q$. Write $t-s-T=N\tau$ with an integer $N\ge1$ and $\tau\in[T,2T]$; such $N$ exists by taking the integer part of $(t-s-T)/T$. For the finitely many intermediate orbit points $Y_{s+T+k\tau}(y)$, $0\le k<N$, choose nearby points $z_k\in\Gamma$; the distance of the late orbit tail to $\Gamma$ tends to zero, since otherwise nested compact tail closures would meet the closed complement of a fixed neighborhood of $\Gamma$. Start the chain at $x_0=p$. The first link of length $T$ ends within $\epsilon/3$ of $z_0$, because $p$ is $\delta$-close to $Y_s(y)$. For $0\le k<N-1$, flow $z_k$ for time $\tau$ and jump to $z_{k+1}$; uniform continuity and the chosen orbit points make each jump less than $\epsilon$. Flow $z_{N-1}$ for time $\tau$ and jump to the exact endpoint $q$, which is $\delta$-close to $Y_t(y)$. This is a finite $(\epsilon,T)$-chain from $p$ to $q$, and all its times lie in $[T,2T]$. Only finitely many nearest-point choices are made for this chain.

Here is a direct finite-graph proof of strong connectivity. Suppose the finite directed graph has more than one strongly connected component. Its finite condensation graph has a terminal component S: starting from any component and following an outgoing edge must stop, since a repeated component would be a directed cycle and hence one strongly connected component. Include in N all vertices and all edges internal to S, and a short terminal segment of every edge entering S from outside. Choose each trimming point in the regular part of that incoming edge. There is no edge leaving S. Thus N is compact and positively invariant relative to Γ, and S is contained in int_Γ N, since all incident half-edges at its vertices are included near those vertices. For every T>0, Φ_T(N)⊂int_Γ N: points of S stay in S, and each added incoming segment moves strictly toward its terminal saddle. No finite-time arrival at that saddle is possible by uniqueness, and its sole outside trimming endpoint moves strictly past the trimming point. Compactness gives δ=dist(Φ_T(N), Γ\int_Γ N)>0. Because N is positively invariant, Φ_t(N)⊂Φ_T(N) for all t≥T. Every (ε,T)-chain in Γ starting in S, for ε<δ, therefore remains in N by induction: the flowed point is in Φ_T(N), and its next jump cannot leave N. There is a vertex outside N, since the terminal component is proper. This contradicts the exact-endpoint internal chain transitivity proved above. Thus all vertices lie in one strongly connected component. This argument controls arbitrarily many jumps and requires no informal claim that a chain itself traces a directed itinerary. For each directed edge $e:v\to w$, choose a finite directed path from $w$ back to $v$; adjoining $e$ gives a closed directed walk. There are finitely many edges, so finitely many such walks cover $\Gamma$. Finiteness comes from the two characteristic outgoing branches per saddle, not from Teschl's theorem. Physical trajectories and their uniqueness/compact-time continuity use [[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]] at C¹. The C¹ Morse coordinates and continuous nonzero branch rate identify exactly two incoming and two outgoing branches; the terminal-component argument uses only compactness, forward orientation and uniqueness. No smooth-only flow or higher regularity of the transformed area density is used.

items.title: Independence of the auxiliary form eta up to exact forms
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation with defining form $\omega$, and let $\eta,\eta'$ be smooth $1$-forms with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega=\eta'\wedge\omega$. If $\eta'-\eta=f\omega$ with $f\in C^\infty(M)$, then $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=\eta\wedge d\eta-d(f\,d\omega)=\eta\wedge d\eta+d(df\wedge\omega)$, and in particular $[\eta'\wedge d\eta']=[\eta\wedge d\eta]$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$.
items.strategy: Write $\eta'=\eta+f\omega$, so $d\eta'=d\eta+df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$ and $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$. Expanding $\eta'\wedge d\eta'-\eta\wedge d\eta$, the terms containing $\eta\wedge\eta$, $d\eta\wedge\omega$, $\omega\wedge d\eta$, $\omega\wedge d\omega$ or $\omega\wedge\omega$ vanish (using $d\eta\wedge\omega=0$ from [[lem-eta-wedge-d-eta-is-closed]] and $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$), leaving $\eta\wedge df\wedge\omega=-df\wedge d\omega=d(df\wedge\omega)$, an exact form. The sign displayed follows from graded commutativity of the two $1$-forms. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Steven Hurder and Remi Langevin, Dynamics and the Godbillon-Vey Class of C1 Foliations (complete author-hosted PDF)
references.locator: §3.1, printed pp. 10-11

items.title: Rescaling the defining form changes the Godbillon-Vey form by an exact form
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation with defining form $\omega$ and $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$. For $\omega'=e^{f}\omega$ with $f\in C^\infty(M)$ one has $d\omega'=\eta'\wedge\omega'$ with $\eta'=\eta+df$, and $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=\eta\wedge d\eta+d(f\,d\eta)$; in particular $[\eta'\wedge d\eta']=[\eta\wedge d\eta]$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. The same conclusion holds for any nowhere-vanishing smooth multiple $\omega'=g\omega$, since on each connected component $g$ is $e^{f}$ or $-e^{f}$.
items.strategy: Compute $d\omega'=e^{f}df\wedge\omega+e^{f}d\omega=e^{f}(df\wedge\omega+\eta\wedge\omega)=(\eta+df)\wedge e^{f}\omega=(\eta+df)\wedge\omega'$, so $\eta'=\eta+df$ is admissible and $d\eta'=d\eta$. Then $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=(\eta+df)\wedge d\eta=\eta\wedge d\eta+d(f\,d\eta)$ because $d(f\,d\eta)=df\wedge d\eta$; the difference is exact and $\eta\wedge d\eta$ is closed by [[lem-eta-wedge-d-eta-is-closed]]. Replacing $\omega$ by $-\omega$ leaves $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$ and $\eta\wedge d\eta$ unchanged, and the general nowhere-vanishing multiple differs from $e^{f}\omega$ by a locally constant sign, so the sign ambiguity is absorbed. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Characteristic-disk singular images can be separated into distinct leaves relative to the boundary collar
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth $3$-manifold, and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a $C^2$ disk map with a prescribed regular boundary collar and finitely many interior nondegenerate characteristic centers and saddles. For every sufficiently small prescribed C² neighborhood of h there is a C² homotopy rel that collar to a map h′ in that neighborhood whose singular points are exactly the original source points, with unchanged transverse-coordinate Hessians and center/saddle types, and whose singular images lie in pairwise distinct ambient leaves. In particular, h′ has no characteristic separatrix joining two distinct singular points; homoclinic separatrices are not excluded.
items.strategy: Enumerate the finite singular set. Around each source point p_i choose disjoint disks V_i away from the fixed collar, with h(cl V_i) inside one C² target box (Y_i,z_i), and choose a smaller W_i around p_i. Write u_i=z_i∘h. Use [[lem-manifold-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]] on the smooth source disk to obtain ρ_i supported in V_i and equal to one near W_i. The compact support of dρ_i misses every critical point, so η_i=min|du_i| there is positive. The vertical interval through h(p_i) meets each previously assigned singular leaf in an at-most-countable set by [[lem-c2-leaf-intersection-with-a-box-transversal-is-countable]]. Their finite union is countable, while every open interval is uncountable by [[cor-interval-uncountable]]. Choose δ_i as small as required, avoiding those leaves, the target chart boundary, and satisfying |δ_i| sup|dρ_i|<η_i/2. Replace the map on V_i by χ_i^{-1}(Y_i,u_i+sδ_iρ_i), 0≤s≤1, and leave it fixed elsewhere. Near p_i the scalar is changed by a constant, so its critical point and Hessian are unchanged. On the transition annulus, |d(u_i+sδ_iρ_i)|≥η_i−|δ_i| sup|dρ_i|>0, so no new critical point occurs. The formula equals h on an open support collar and is C² by [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]. Disjoint supports preserve earlier choices. Allocate a finite C² error budget and reparametrize each stage to be stationary near its endpoints before concatenating. Every choice after obtaining the countable atlas is finite. A characteristic trajectory maps into one leaf; a terminal tail in an endpoint box lies in one constant-transverse-coordinate plaque and its limit lies in that same plaque. Thus a connection between distinct singular points would put their images in the same ambient leaf, contrary to the separation. This supplies genericity input only; it proves neither a minimal cycle nor frontier/ranking or a transverse endpoint fence.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (local C² plaque-chain adaptation)
references.locator: §4.2 chart/plaque/holonomy pattern; coded countability and relative perturbation supplied locally

items.title: A C² first-integral period annulus has a C² leaf product
items.statement: Assume ACω. Let A⊂R² be a connected open set carrying a C² first-integral atlas: each chart has a C² submersion u, its connected levels are the leaves, and overlap transverse coordinates differ by C² local diffeomorphisms. Suppose all leaves are simple compact C² circles whose bounded Jordan domains are strictly nested, with consistent orientation. Then A is an open annulus, and there is a C² diffeomorphism Ψ:S¹×(0,1)→A taking each circle onto one leaf and increasing in the nested leaf order. For any nowhere-zero C¹ tangent generator X, orient θ so $\Psi^{-1}_*X=a(s,\theta)\partial_\theta$ with a positive C¹ function a. No θ-independent speed, C² flow of X, or C² coefficient a is asserted. The atlas applies to u=z∘h for C² characteristic maps on their regular annulus.
items.strategy:
Near a compact leaf C choose a short C² transverse interval σ inside a first-integral box, and shrink it so it is transverse to the line field everywhere. Orient each circle as the boundary of its bounded Jordan domain, using the consistent orientation in the hypotheses. Along σ the determinant of a locally chosen positively oriented tangent and σ′ is continuous and nonzero, hence has one sign. Consequently all intersections of any fixed leaf circle with this particular σ have the same inward/outward crossing direction. On the compact section subarc between two hypothetical intersections, transversality makes intersections isolated and finite, while the Jordan separation conclusion of [[lem-finitely-cornered-regular-plane-curve-separates-without-choice]] makes entry and exit crossings alternate. Thus this section meets each circle at most once. This argument uses everywhere-transversality and consistent boundary orientation; it makes no sign assertion for an arbitrary curve. Cover C by a finite cyclic chain of C² foliated rectangles. Finite plaque transport defines a C² return map H on a smaller interval in σ. Its returned point lies on the same global circle as the starting point and on σ, so the just-proved uniqueness of section intersection gives H(t)=t. Mere proximity in the starting box would not suffice to identify two plaques. Identity holonomy now makes the transported transverse parameter a well-defined C² first integral on the local saturated neighborhood.

Here is the finite phase gluing. Choose a C² once-around parametrization $\gamma_0:S^1\to C$ and a finite cyclic cover by plaque arcs whose slightly enlarged arcs lie in the chosen rectangles; refine so only adjacent enlarged arcs overlap and each overlap lies in a common rectangle. In each rectangle, hold its transported transverse coordinate fixed at $t$ and keep the reference leaf-coordinate of $\gamma_0$ fixed. This gives a C² candidate $\gamma_i(t,\theta)$ on the enlarged arc. On an adjacent overlap express both candidates in the common plaque coordinate $x$; they have the same transverse coordinate and agree as functions of $\theta$ at $t=0$. Choose a C² cutoff $\chi$ equal to one on an open collar at one end and zero on an open collar at the other, and set $x(t,\theta)=\chi(\theta)x_i(t,\theta)+(1-\chi(\theta))x_{i+1}(t,\theta)$. The point with plaque coordinate $x(t,\theta)$ and the shared transverse coordinate remains on that leaf. At $t=0$, both candidates equal $\gamma_0$, so $\partial_\theta x$ is the positive reference derivative; compactness of the finitely many closed overlaps lets us shrink the transverse interval once so $\partial_\theta x>0$ on every blend. On the two open collars the formula equals the corresponding candidate exactly, so adjacent pieces and all their derivatives agree there. The cyclic product closes because $H$ is the identity. Thus the resulting $\gamma(t,\cdot)$ is a C² regular circle map, positive in phase, and of degree one: the finitely many oriented plaque arcs are traversed once in their cyclic order, and their exact collar transitions preserve that order. Each $\gamma_t$ is a local diffeomorphism into its connected compact leaf, hence is onto; degree one makes it one-to-one. Since $t$ is a submersion, $(t,\theta)\mapsto\gamma(t,\theta)$ is a C² local diffeomorphism and is a C² product over a neighborhood of the leaf.

For the global base, quotient $A$ by its circle leaves. The local products make the quotient map open and give increasing C² interval charts. Disjoint compact leaves have disjoint sufficiently small saturated product collars, so the quotient $B$ is Hausdorff. Images of a countable basis of $A$ form a countable basis of $B$; $B$ is connected and has no endpoints. The nested leaf order agrees with its interval-chart topology. A bounded nonempty subset has a supremum: if its order cut had no least upper bound, the lower and upper sides of the cut would be disjoint nonempty open sets separating connected $B$. Every closed order segment $[a,b]$ is compact by the open-cover supremum proof: for an open cover let $S$ be the points $x$ for which $[a,x]$ has a finite subcover. A cover member at $a$ makes $S$ nonempty; if $c=\sup S<b$, a cover member containing $c$ extends a finite subcover past $c$, a contradiction, while if $c=b$ that same member finishes a finite cover of $[a,b]$.

Apply [[thm-second-countable-implies-lindelof]] with ACω to select countably many local product charts with precompact interval cores. Their finite order hulls exhaust $B$. Replace the exhaustion by a strictly expanding one: at each step take the least later finite hull extending both endpoints of the previous hull. On each compact shell choose a finite cover by precompact interval charts and explicit C² bumps $\eta((t-t_i)/r_i)$, where $\eta(v)=e^{-1/(1-v^2)}$ for $|v|<1$ and zero outside. Choose each support inside the next shell; the family is locally finite. Normalizing its positive sum gives a C² partition of unity. For increasing local coordinates $t_i$, $\alpha=\sum_i\rho_i\,dt_i$ is a positive C¹ one-form. Apply [[cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function]] in each interval chart to the positive C¹ coefficient of $\alpha$; each local primitive is C² because its derivative is C¹. On overlaps the primitives differ by constants, so fixing one value and continuing across the compact order segments gives a strictly increasing C² local diffeomorphism $B\to J$ onto an open interval; injectivity follows from the leaf order and the image is an interval by connectedness. An explicit increasing smooth reparametrization takes $J$ to $(0,1)$.

Choose a countable locally finite chain of compact base slabs inside the selected product intervals, with consecutive open overlap collars. Select the local products, seams and transition lifts together using ACω before gluing. On an overlap the transition is a C² family $g_s$ of orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphisms; lift it to $G(s,\theta+2\pi)=G(s,\theta)+2\pi$ fixing one seam value. Extend over the next slab by $G_{\rm ext}(s,\theta)=\chi(s)G(s,\theta)+(1-\chi(s))G(s_*,\theta)$, with a fixed C² cutoff equal to one on the old-side open collar and zero before the overlap ends. Its $\theta$ derivative is a convex combination of positive derivatives. Compose with the already-built lift before each extension. This is deterministic recursion along the preselected chain; local finiteness and exact collar agreement give a global C² product. Fiberwise bijectivity and the local C² inverses prove it is a C² diffeomorphism. Because $D\Psi^{-1}$ and $X\circ\Psi$ are C¹, the tangent coefficient is C¹; connectedness permits one global phase orientation making it positive. This is a foliation-atlas product, not a constant-speed phase obtained from a C¹ flow.

The construction proves the stronger connected-open-set formulation just stated; a pre-existing annulus homeomorphism is never used. In particular the quotient is Hausdorff because two distinct compact leaves have disjoint saturated collars: choose disjoint small Euclidean neighborhoods of the leaves, then shrink each finite local product uniformly so its entire circle fibers lie in its prescribed neighborhood. The quotient map is open because the saturation of an open subset in each local product is open. Thus the images of a countable Euclidean basis are a countable basis. A missing cut point would split the connected quotient into its two open order rays; and the supremum open-cover proof gives compact order segments. The selected local product cores have compact closures strictly inside their full product intervals. All later auxiliary data must be selected without dependent choice: after choosing the countable product system by ACω, enumerate its cores, take finite order hulls, and pass to the least later hull extending both endpoints. These compact hulls exhaust the base because each quotient point is in a core. For each compact shell the set of admissible finite coordinate covers, bumps and positive-form data is nonempty by compactness and the displayed explicit bump. Use ACω once for this countable family of nonempty finite-data sets. After integrating the resulting positive C¹ one-form, use ACω on the countable family of finite slab covers, orientation-preserving local product charts and adjacent transition lifts. The real base coordinate makes rational subdivisions available. One can insist on precompact overlap collars, threefold or finer refinements so every seam lies in a common local product, and a locally finite chain of slabs. The choices are all made before phase gluing, and the later recursion is the specified cutoff formula on that preselected chain, not a repeated selection dependent on the previously glued map. Each extension is made relative to an open seam collar. The product is therefore C², its inverse is C² by the scalar-root inverse supplier, and A is an annulus as a conclusion. This supplies exactly the connected nested family needed in the frontier application.

items.title: Positive transverse accessibility is a preorder and mutual accessibility is an equivalence relation
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use [[def-positive-transverse-accessibility-between-leaves]] for a C² cooriented foliation on a smooth manifold without boundary. If a genuine nonempty positive transverse segment joins leaves A to B, then for any x∈A and y∈B there is such a segment from x to y. This endpoint conclusion is not asserted merely from the formal A=B clause. The relation $\succeq_F$ is reflexive and transitive, hence a preorder. The relation $A\sim_F B$ defined by $A\succeq_F B$ and $B\succeq_F A$ is an equivalence relation on the set of leaves.
items.strategy:
Endpoint adjustment: a finite plaque chain joins any two points of one leaf; [[cor-components-of-open-subsets-of-rn-are-polygonally-connected]] supplies finite chartwise leaf paths. Smooth their finitely many corners inside convex plaque charts to obtain C² leaf paths γ_A from x to the original initial point and γ_B from the original terminal point to y. Let α be the given positive segment. On the compact union of these three paths choose finitely many smooth ambient chart bumps by [[lem-manifold-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]. In each smooth ambient chart a constant vector is positive for the continuous cooriented tangent planes on a sufficiently small neighborhood. A finite bump sum yields a smooth positive transverse field X near that union. Similarly patch the local C¹ positive annihilating forms of the C² atlas to a C¹ form ω with kerω=TF. The local smooth flow φ of X is supplied by [[thm-fundamental-theorem-on-flows]]; finite indexed compactness from [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]] gives a uniform interval and derivative bounds. On that compact flow neighborhood ω(X)≥b>0. For each leaf path γ, put v(s,a)=ω(Dφ_a γ′(s)); v(s,0)=0 and the continuous ∂_a v is uniformly bounded on the compact parameter set; [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] gives |v(s,a)|≤A|a|. Choose B>A/b. On the initial leaf path use a(s)=δ(e^{Bs}−1)/B; on the terminal leaf path use a(s)=−δ(e^{B(1−s)}−1)/B. In both cases a′=B|a|+δ and ω((φ_a γ)′)≥−A|a|+b a′>0. The initial and final offsets are zero, so endpoints remain exactly x,y. Along α join the positive offset at its start to the negative offset at its end by a fixed C² profile scaled by δ. Since min ω(α′)>0, the O(δ) perturbation of its derivative remains positive for small δ. Thus the three pieces form a piecewise C² positive path with the desired endpoints.

At each internal seam choose one C² foliated chart. The one-sided transverse-coordinate derivatives have a positive lower bound c on a small compact interval. Mollify the continuous piecewise C² chart curve with a nonnegative kernel; the mollified transverse derivative is still ≥c. Blend using a cutoff supported near the seam. Its extra transverse derivative is ρ′(z_moll−z), which tends uniformly to zero; choose the radius so it is <c/2. The result is C² and positive, agrees with the original pieces on open end collars, and retains x,y. Finite compatible gluing has the regularity of [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]. This proves endpoint adjustment whenever α really exists. For transitivity, discard formal-equality cases; otherwise adjust the B→C segment to start at the endpoint of the A→B segment, concatenate and smooth its one internal seam in the same way. Reflexivity is the defining equality clause, so [[def-preorder]] applies. Mutual accessibility is reflexive and symmetric by definition; two applications of preorder transitivity prove its transitivity, giving [[def-equivalence-relation]]. The construction uses only finitely many choices and local flows, not a recursively chosen sequence or full AC.

references.title: S. P. Novikov, The Topology of Foliations, English translation by J. A. Zilber
references.locator: §1, Definition1.4 and Lemma1.1, printed p.2; mutual-accessibility component definition immediately following Lemma1.1

items.title: A fixed cap product glues by unique transverse flow roots
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. Given a C² leafwise cap B:W→L on a compact source disk, a fixed smooth transverse field V near its image, and finite holonomy-trivial cap continuation, there is a jointly C² transverse product P(x,t) obtained by unique short V-flow roots of the transported leaf label. If the prescribed collar trace projects along V to B and its transported parameter range lies in the uniform interval, then P(x,t_C(x)) equals that trace pointwise on the full collar.
items.strategy:
A cap gives an actual globally compatible transverse product

The earlier local-center-saddle memo's instruction to keep the plaque coordinates of B(x) in every box is not literally a gluing proof: transverse chart transitions can change plaque coordinates. Equality of transverse holonomy values implies equality of leaf labels, not equality of points. Here is a repair.

For one C² cap B:W→L, choose a smooth positively transverse ambient vector field V on a neighborhood of the compact image. Finite local positive fields and a smooth partition of unity give V; positivity is an open convex condition. Its flow Φ_s is smooth. Choose finitely many boxes and a finite subdivision of W subordinate to their inverse images. Tree continuation gives a leaf label z_i(t) in each box. The finitely many remaining edge relations are identity holonomy germs because their B-images are nullhomotopic in L: they come from loops of the parameter disk. Shrink to one common interval where all relations agree as maps.

On each box solve

    z_i(Φ_s(B(x))) = z_i(t)

for the unique small s=s_i(x,t). Its left derivative with respect to s is nonzero. The C² inverse-function theorem and compactness give a uniform interval and a jointly C² solution. On overlaps the two equations specify the same leaf label on the same short V orbit; uniqueness gives exactly the same s. Thus P(x,t)=Φ_{s(x,t)}(B(x)) glues pointwise and in both derivatives. For fixed t its points lie in one leaf by the finite continuation relations, and ∂_tP is transverse. No immersion or injectivity of B is needed.

To obtain the exact old collar, first define B there by projecting f(x) along that same V orbit to the endpoint leaf label. This projection is C² by the identical scalar-root argument. Extend B across the source interior using the single fixed leafwise cap, flattening its seam in an open collar. On the source circuit Γ the section t_C is zero. Construct P on a fixed enlarged block before thinning the exterior collar; compactness then puts its actual section range inside P's interval. Uniqueness of the scalar root gives f(x)=P(x,t_C(x)) exactly on that thinner collar. This fixes both the old nonzero-range issue and the pointwise overlap issue. The statement needs the supplied projection collar; an arbitrary prechosen B and arbitrary nearby f need not lie on the same V orbits.

references.title: Mark Brittenham, Foliations and the Topology of 3-manifolds, class 11
references.locator: Class 11 pp.1–3 motivates finite induction; complete new port construction is local, in the companion memo

items.title: A one-quadrant homoclinic disk contains a center
items.statement: Let X be the characteristic C¹ field of a C² characteristic disk with finitely many nondegenerate centers and saddles. Let K be the bounded source disk of a simple directed homoclinic circuit through a saddle q. Suppose K occupies precisely one of the four local saddle sectors at q. If c_K and s_K count the centers and saddles strictly inside K, then c_K−s_K=1. In particular K contains a center. The saddle q is not included in s_K.
items.strategy: Cut the circuit at two regular sections in a sufficiently small saddle box. In that box the local transverse first integral u has a nondegenerate saddle and the one-sector component of u−u(q) of the appropriate sign is bounded by the two chosen separatrix branches. Replace the corner by a small regular level arc in that sector. The implicit-function theorem gives a C² arc up to both section collars. Push the remaining compact regular circuit slightly into K, matching the two collars; in finitely many regular first-integral charts the pushed arc can be chosen so that X has positive component along its directed tangent. Near the joining collars this is preserved by sufficiently small C¹ interpolation. The resulting closed curve C lies in K, bounds all its interior zeros, excludes q, and its directed unit tangent has positive inner product with either X/|X| everywhere or its negative everywhere. Thus the straight homotopy between the normalized field and that directed tangent is nonzero. The tangent of this rounded simple curve has degree 1 with the positive boundary orientation (reversing both tangent directions changes the angle by the constant π and not its degree). This can be proved by the finite polygonal turning argument after polygonizing its regular arcs in disjoint tubular collars. The same punctured-polygon argument as the characteristic index-count supplier now gives c_K−s_K=deg(X|C)=1. No assertion about the three-sector outer loop or the two-sector pinched region follows from this calculation.

references.title: Mark Brittenham, Foliations and the Topology of 3-manifolds; local refinements of class 11
references.locator: Class 11, finite center/saddle extraction; complete local construction in the strategy

items.statement: A based loop in a C² surface is based-homotopic to a regular C² immersed loop having only finitely many transverse double points and no triple points; all construction choices are finite or countable.
items.title: Finite general position for a leafwise loop
items.strategy:
Cover the compact original loop by finitely many coordinate disks and subdivide its parameter circle so successive pieces lie in these disks. Replace each piece by a finite coordinate-polygonal path with the same endpoints; convex coordinate homotopies give the specified homotopy. Perturb the finitely many vertices and directions to remove constant pieces and retracing adjacent tangents, keeping the basepoint fixed. Round corners in disjoint source intervals using coordinate convolution and a cutoff on straight tails. One coordinate remains strictly increasing across each rounded corner, so the curve is regular. This yields a regular C² curve; compactness gives a uniform source neighborhood of the diagonal on which no two distinct parameters have equal images.

For source pairs outside that neighborhood, choose a finite product-box cover, each pair of disjoint source intervals mapping into one surface coordinate disk whenever their images can coincide. Use finitely many C² bump perturbations supported in these source intervals, with two independent coordinate displacement parameters on each smaller interval. At any equality of two branches, the parameter derivative of their coordinate difference has rank2. The universal equality set is thus a C² manifold; projection to the finite parameter space has equal source and target dimensions. Sard’s equal-dimensional clause makes its critical values null; choose a parameter outside the finitely many critical-value sets. At that parameter every double point is transverse. The same independent branch parameters make the triple-equality set have source dimension one less than parameter dimension, so Sard excludes all triple points. Work on the finitely many compact pair/triple boxes; if smaller open cores are required, use a fixed countable rational exhaustion and avoid the resulting countable union of null sets. This uses at most ACω, not a family of choices indexed by all curve points. The transverse double-pair set is compact (away from the excluded diagonal neighborhood) and discrete, hence finite. Small perturbations preserve regularity and the based homotopy by the coordinate straight-line homotopies. The only prescribed basepoint can be retained, and generic directions of other branches avoid it.

items.title: A noncompact leaf meets a positive closed transversal at C2 regularity
items.statement: Assume ACω. In a C² cooriented codimension-one foliation of a closed three-manifold, every intrinsically noncompact leaf meets a positive closed transversal. The transversal can be chosen to avoid any specified finite family of distinct compact leaves. Conversely, absence of such a transversal forces intrinsic compactness.

references.title: S. P. Novikov, The Topology of Foliations (complete English translation)
references.locator: §1 Lemma1.2; the finite C² box construction and barrier avoidance are proved below

items.strategy:
Take a finite foliation-box cover of compact M, with smaller cores still covering it. If the leaf met only finitely many plaques in each box, its intersection with that box would be a finite union of whole plaques, closed relative to the box. It would therefore be closed in M and locally embedded, with its intrinsic topology equal to the ambient subspace topology; compactness of M would make it intrinsically compact. Consequently some box contains infinitely many distinct leaf plaques. If compact barriers are prescribed, each barrier meets finitely many plaques in a sufficiently refined finite cover (compact leaves are embedded); one transverse interval in that box, avoiding their finitely many plaque values, contains two distinct plaques of the given leaf. Choose their points on one short vertical transversal at levels a<b. Connect the point at b to the point at a by a finite C² leafwise path; a connected surface is path connected by its local chart balls and the usual open-and-closed path-reachability argument. The compact path avoids every barrier, so a finite tubular neighborhood of it also avoids them.

Finite plaque transport gives a C² transverse strip P(r,s) along this path for uniformly small s, with each r-track positively transverse and the s=0 path the chosen leafwise path. In a chart its transverse label is an increasing function of s independent of r when s is constant. Choose s(r)=δ₀+δr with δ>0 small; the curve P(r,s(r)) therefore has strictly positive transverse derivative. Its two endpoints stay arbitrarily close to the original levels b and a. Choose δ₀,δ sufficiently small so its final level is still below b and its initial level is above b. Close it by the positive vertical interval from its end back to its start. That interval crosses the original leaf plaque at b, so the closed curve meets the given leaf. Smooth the finitely many joining corners inside chart balls, preserving the open cone of positive transverse tangent vectors and the avoidance of the compact barriers. This supplies a positive closed C² immersed transversal. If an embedded circle is desired, finite small coordinate perturbations remove all its self-intersections in dimension three: regularize finite polygonal arcs and choose vertices outside the finitely many equality constraints for disjoint parameter pieces, then round their corners; the one-dimensional diagonal remains injective by regularity, and sufficiently small C¹ changes preserve positivity and the chosen crossing. No arbitrary family of point choices or full-AC smooth global-stability result is used. The contrapositive gives the final clause.

The last generic embedding step may equivalently be performed with finite independent three-coordinate bump parameters on disjoint source intervals. The equality map of two branches is a submersion in these parameters. Away from a fixed diagonal neighborhood its zero manifold has dimension one less than the finite parameter space; its projection has only critical values, hence a null image by the declared Euclidean Sard clause. A finite chart cover, or one fixed countable rational exhaustion of its open cores, therefore admits parameters excluding all off-diagonal equalities. The derivative remains regular under small C¹ perturbation, giving diagonal injectivity. Retain one small vertical crossing segment at b and keep all other perturbations supported away from it. This justifies the embedded-circle option without assuming that arbitrary coordinate arcs in different charts are straight segments in one global Euclidean space.

items.title: The Godbillon-Vey class of a codimension-one foliation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$, let $\omega$ be a nowhere-vanishing defining $1$-form with $TF=\ker\omega$, and let $\eta$ be a smooth $1$-form with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, whose existence is guaranteed by [[lem-frobenius-divisibility-gives-d-omega-equals-eta-wedge-omega]]. The **Godbillon-Vey class** of $F$ is $\mathrm{GV}(F):=[\eta\wedge d\eta]\in H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. It is well defined: $\eta\wedge d\eta$ is closed ([[lem-eta-wedge-d-eta-is-closed]]), and the class is unchanged by replacing $\eta$ by $\eta+f\omega$ ([[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-independent-of-the-choice-of-eta-up-to-an-exact-form]]) and by rescaling $\omega$ ([[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-invariant-under-rescaling-the-defining-form]]). Only the de Rham class over $\mathbb R$ is named; no integral refinement is defined on this page.
items.strategy: This is the standard definition of the Godbillon-Vey class for a co-oriented codimension-one foliation: existence of $\eta$, closedness of $\eta\wedge d\eta$, and independence of both auxiliary choices are exactly the three divisibility lemmas listed, so the class is a well-defined element of $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. It is the secondary-class companion of the characteristic classes of chern-weil-theory-and-characteristic-forms and requires at least $C^2$ regularity of the foliation.

references.title: Steven Hurder and Remi Langevin, Dynamics and the Godbillon-Vey Class of C1 Foliations (complete author-hosted PDF)

items.title: One-sided trivial-holonomy classes form a normal subgroup
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, $L$ a leaf, $x\in L$, and $j$ one of its two sides. The classes in $\pi_1(L,x)$ whose one-sided holonomy germ is the identity form a normal subgroup $N_j(L,x)\triangleleft\pi_1(L,x)$. Consequently the quotient $P_j(L,x)=\pi_1(L,x)/N_j(L,x)$ used to define ordinary one-sided limit cycles is a group.
items.strategy: The holonomy representation restricts, by transverse orientation, to a group homomorphism from $\pi_1(L,x)$ to the group of side-preserving germs of local diffeomorphisms of a half-transversal. Its kernel is exactly the classes with identity one-sided holonomy. Kernels are normal subgroups, so $N_j$ is normal and the quotient $P_j$ is defined.

items.title: A compact leafwise nullhomotopy persists under a transverse deformation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ regular foliation, and let $H:S^1\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M$ be a $C^2$ trace annulus such that each loop $H_s=H(\cdot,s)$ lies in a single leaf and every point track $s\mapsto H(\theta,s)$ is transverse to $F$. If $H_{s_0}$ is null-homotopic in its leaf by a compact continuous disk map, then $H_s$ is null-homotopic in its leaf for all $s$ in some open interval about $s_0$.
items.strategy:
Shrink the parameter interval about $s_0$ so the compact image of one fixed null disk $u:D^2\to L_{s_0}$ and the prescribed trace annulus lie in finitely many regular foliated boxes. The transport argument uses the original compact continuous disk and makes no smoothing assertion. Choose a base point $x_0\in\partial D^2$ and use the transverse track $s\mapsto H(x_0,s)$ as the parameter transversal. Triangulate $D^2$ finely enough that each closed simplex maps into a single plaque of a foliated box. Along each oriented edge, plaque continuation defines a local transport between endpoint transversals. For the finite transport step, choose a spanning tree of the triangulated 1-skeleton rooted at $x_0$, and transport to each vertex along its unique tree path. For each of the finitely many edges outside the tree, the tree path to its initial vertex, followed by that edge and the reverse tree path from its terminal vertex, is a loop in $D^2$. It is nullhomotopic in $D^2$, so composing its nullhomotopy with $u$ shows that its holonomy germ is the identity. Include also the finitely many 2-simplex boundary loops; each is filled by $u$ on that simplex and has identity holonomy. Intersect these finitely many identity neighborhoods and chart domains to obtain one interval $J$. The tree transports then agree across every edge and around every triangle on $J$. In each simplex, extend the edge transport in plaque coordinates while holding the transverse coordinate fixed. These compatible local extensions give a continuous disk $u_s:D^2\to L_s$ and its transported boundary loop $G_s$ for each $s\in J$; only the one fixed disk is transported, with no varying fillings or limiting disks.

To identify the boundary, for each $x\in\partial D^2$ fix an arc $q_x$ from $x_0$ to $x$. The boundary transport defining $G_s(x)$ is plaque continuation from $H_s(x_0)$ along the fixed path $u|q_x=H_{s_0}|q_x$. The prescribed family $H|_{q_x\times J}$ gives the same continuation: on each member of a finite chart subdivision of this square, the path direction is tangent to the plaques, so its transverse coordinate is constant along the path; at chart changes the coordinate changes by the same plaque-transition map. Consequently $G_s(x)$ and $H_s(x)$ have the same transverse coordinate in every common terminal chart. They lie in the same local plaque there, and the pointwise plaque segments give a plaque-wise homotopy between the two boundary loops. The construction is uniform in $x$ after a finite subdivision of $S^1$ and shrinking $J$, by compactness of the trace and [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]. With coherent continuation along the chosen boundary arcs the endpoints agree, so this homotopy may be taken constant; equivalently, attach its plaque-wise boundary collar to $u_s$ to obtain a disk whose boundary is exactly $H_s$. This proves openness from one compact filling only and does not assert persistence for varying disks or transport across a saddle polycycle. The C² regularity of specified plaque transports and compatible open-collar gluings is supplied by [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]; this does not assert existence of a saddle endpoint family.

items.title: A fixed leafwise cap gives a joint transverse product with exact collar data
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ codimension-one regular foliation of a $3$-manifold $M$, let $W$ be a compact disk, and let $B:W\to L$ be a $C^2$ map into one leaf. Fix $x_*\in W$ and a $C^2$ transversal $\tau:(-\delta,\delta)\to M$ through $B(x_*)$. Plaque continuation of $\tau$ along $B\circ q$, for a path $q$ from $x_*$ to $x$, is independent of $q$ near $t=0$ because $B$ maps the simply connected disk into one leaf; write $T_x(t)$ for the endpoint in the fixed transported transversal at $B(x)$. There are a uniform interval $J=(-r,r)$ and a jointly $C^2$ map $P:W\times J\to M$ with $P(x,0)=B(x)$, leaf-valued slices $P(\cdot,t)$ and transverse tracks $P(x,\cdot)$, such that $$dP^{-1}(TF)=TW=\ker(dt).$$ Let $C\subseteq W$ be a prescribed collar region with a $C^2$ trace $f_C$ and its actual holonomy-trivialized section $t_C$, so $f_C(x)=T_x(t_C(x))$. If a smaller closed collar $C_0\subseteq C$ has compact section range $S=t_C(C_0)\Subset J$, choose an open interval $I$ with $S\Subset I\Subset J$. Then the restriction of $P$ to $W\times I$ satisfies $P(x,t_C(x))=f_C(x)$ pointwise on $C_0$ and its interior. The boundary section may be nonzero. If $C$ is a collar of $\partial W$ and $t_C=0$ there, continuity gives such a $C_0$ as a special case. The uniform interval is constructed from the fixed cap before the actual section range is checked.
items.strategy:
A cap gives an actual globally compatible transverse product

The earlier local-center-saddle memo's instruction to keep the plaque coordinates of B(x) in every box is not literally a gluing proof: transverse chart transitions can change plaque coordinates. Equality of transverse holonomy values implies equality of leaf labels, not equality of points. Here is a repair.

For one C² cap B:W→L, choose a smooth positively transverse ambient vector field V on a neighborhood of the compact image. Finite local positive fields and a smooth partition of unity give V; positivity is an open convex condition. Its flow Φ_s is smooth. Choose finitely many boxes and a finite subdivision of W subordinate to their inverse images. Tree continuation gives a leaf label z_i(t) in each box. The finitely many remaining edge relations are identity holonomy germs because their B-images are nullhomotopic in L: they come from loops of the parameter disk. Shrink to one common interval where all relations agree as maps.

On each box solve

    z_i(Φ_s(B(x))) = z_i(t)

for the unique small s=s_i(x,t). Its left derivative with respect to s is nonzero. The C² inverse-function theorem and compactness give a uniform interval and a jointly C² solution. On overlaps the two equations specify the same leaf label on the same short V orbit; uniqueness gives exactly the same s. Thus P(x,t)=Φ_{s(x,t)}(B(x)) glues pointwise and in both derivatives. For fixed t its points lie in one leaf by the finite continuation relations, and ∂_tP is transverse. No immersion or injectivity of B is needed.

To obtain the exact old collar, first define B there by projecting f(x) along that same V orbit to the endpoint leaf label. This projection is C² by the identical scalar-root argument. Extend B across the source interior using the single fixed leafwise cap, flattening its seam in an open collar. On the source circuit Γ the section t_C is zero. Construct P on a fixed enlarged block before thinning the exterior collar; compactness then puts its actual section range inside P's interval. Uniqueness of the scalar root gives f(x)=P(x,t_C(x)) exactly on that thinner collar. This fixes both the old nonzero-range issue and the pointwise overlap issue. The statement needs the supplied projection collar; an arbitrary prechosen B and arbitrary nearby f need not lie on the same V orbits.

references.locator: §6, printed pp.16–19 (fixed-disk transport setting); joint C² transport and compact-range exact-collar adaptation are supplied locally in the center–saddle carrier memo

items.title: A flat transverse drift realizes the period-annulus frontier as an omega-limit set
items.statement: Let $X$ be a $C^1$ planar vector field on an open neighborhood of a compact disk $D$, and let $\Psi:S^1\times(0,1)\to A\subset\operatorname{int}D$ be a given $C^2$ leaf product (as supplied by [[lem-c2-first-integral-period-annuli-have-c2-products]]), with $X=a(s,\theta)\partial_\theta$ and a positive $C^1$ coefficient $a$. Assume the periodic curves $C_s=\Psi(S^1\times\{s\})$ bound nested Jordan domains $D_s$ and $\Gamma=\partial\bigcup_{0<s<1}\operatorname{int}(D_s)$ is compact. Then there is a $C^1$ vector field $Y$ on a neighborhood of $D$ that equals $X$ on $\Gamma$ and off an outer subannulus and has a positive orbit $y$ with $\omega_Y^+(y)=\Gamma$. The construction uses no choice principle.
items.strategy:
Put Ω_s=int D_s and Ω=⋃_{0<s<1}Ω_s, so Γ=∂Ω as in the hypotheses. Strict nesting gives cl Ω_s⊂Ω_t for s<t and C_s⊂Ω_t. Here is the complete Hausdorff exhaustion argument. For r∈(0,1) set T_r=cl(⋃_{s≥r}C_s), a nonempty compact subset of D. These sets decrease with r. Every C_s is in Ω, so their tail intersection K∞ is contained in cl Ω. If x∈Ω_t, a ball about x lies in Ω_t, and every C_s with s>t avoids that ball; hence K∞∩Ω=∅. Thus K∞⊂Γ. For any ε>0, if arbitrarily late C_s had points at distance ≥ε from Γ, the nested compact sets T_r∩{x∈D:dist(x,Γ)≥ε} would all be nonempty and have a common point, contrary to K∞⊂Γ. This proves sup_{x∈C_s}dist(x,Γ)→0. Conversely fix p∈Γ and ε>0. Choose x∈Ω∩B_{ε/2}(p) and t with x∈Ω_t. For s>t, x∈Ω_s while p∉Ω_s; along the segment from x to p, the boundary C_s is met, at a point within ε/2 of p. Cover compact Γ by finitely many balls B_{ε/2}(p_i), make these finitely many choices x_i,t_i, and take s>max t_i. Then every point of Γ is within ε of C_s. Consequently C_s→Γ in Hausdorff distance, and Γ⊂cl A. These are finite choices for each ε, not a chosen sequence of witnesses.

Choose $s_1\in(0,1)$ and put $m(s)=\min_\theta a(s,\theta)>0$, $L(s)=\max_\theta\|\partial_s\Psi(s,\theta)\|$, and $q(s)=\min\{(1-s)^2,(1-s)^2m(s)/(1+L(s))\}$. These functions are continuous and $q$ is positive on compact subintervals. Write $\tau(s)=\log((1-s_1)/(1-s))$. With $\eta(t)=\exp(-1/(1-t^2))$ for $|t|<1$ and $\eta=0$ otherwise, set $\rho_n(s)=\eta(\tau(s)-n-\tfrac12)/\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(\tau(s)-j-\tfrac12)$. This is an explicit smooth locally finite partition with uniformly finite overlap, positive sum, and active indices tending to infinity as $s\to1$. Regard these bands on the half-closed interval $[s_1,1)$: the $n=0$ support may include $s_1$, where $\Psi$ is already defined; every support is therefore a compact subset of $(0,1)$. For each support let $B_n=\Psi(S^1\times\operatorname{supp}\rho_n)$, $d_n=\operatorname{dist}(B_n,\Gamma)>0$, $q_n=\min_{\operatorname{supp}\rho_n}q>0$, and $M_n=1+\sup_{B_n}(|\rho_nW|+\|D(\rho_nW)\|)$ for $W=\Psi_*\partial_s$, with the derivative taken in ambient coordinates. For clarity, any continuous real function on a nonempty compact metric set is bounded by the finite-subcover argument applied to the inverse images of $(-n,n)$. Its supremum is attained: the closed nonempty sets $\{x:f(x)\ge\sup f-1/n\}$ are nested, so compactness gives a common point; apply the same argument to $-f$ for the minimum. Thus $m(s)$ and $L(s)$ attain their extrema on the phase circle. Their continuity in $s$ follows from uniform continuity on a compact phase neighborhood and $|\min f-\min g|,|\max f-\max g|\le\sup|f-g|$. Each $B_n$ is compact; the distance to the compact disjoint $\Gamma$ is a positive 1-Lipschitz function there, so its minimum $d_n$ is attained and positive. The continuous positive $q$ attains a positive minimum $q_n$ on each compact support, and the continuous ambient $C^1$ norm of $\rho_nW$ has finite maximum $M_n-1$ on $B_n$. These extrema are uniquely specified real numbers; no sequence of witnesses is selected. Set $c_n=2^{-n-1}\min(q_n,d_n/M_n)$ and $b_0=\sum_{n\ge0}c_n\rho_n$. Then $b_0>0$, $b_0\le q$, and the summands $V_n=c_n\rho_nW$ satisfy both $|V_n(z)|\le2^{-n-1}\operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)$ and $\|DV_n(z)\|\le2^{-n-1}d_n$. Uniform finite overlap and cofinal active indices give $V=b_0W=o(\operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma))$ and $DV\to0$ as $z\to\Gamma$. Thus extension by zero across $\Gamma$ is $C^1$ with derivative zero there. Multiply $b_0$ by one fixed smooth cutoff flat at $s_1$, positive for $s>s_1$ and equal to one near $1$, to extend by zero across the inner edge as well. The band functions are explicit; no countable selection is used.

Put $Y=X+b(s)\partial_s$ on the outer subannulus and $Y=X$ elsewhere. It is $C^1$, equals $X$ with the same derivative on $\Gamma$, and has no new zero in the drift region. Along an orbit, $\dot s=b(s)$, $\dot\theta=a(s,\theta)$, so
$$
\frac{ds}{d\theta}\le\frac{(1-s)^2}{1+L(s)},\qquad
\int_{s_2}^{s}\frac{du}{b(u)}\ge\int_{s_2}^{s}\frac{du}{(1-u)^2}\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
\theta(s)-\theta(s_2)\ge\int_{s_2}^{s}\frac{1+L(u)}{(1-u)^2}\,du\longrightarrow\infty.
$$
Hence the orbit tends to $s=1$ only at infinite time and makes infinitely many full phase turns, even if $m(s)\to0$. Over each unit phase turn starting at $s_k$, integrate $ds/d\theta\le(1-s)^2/(1+L(s))$: monotonicity of $s$ gives $s-s_k\le(1-s_k)^2$, and $\int_{s_k}^{s}L(u)\,du=\int L(s(\theta))(ds/d\theta)\,d\theta\le(1-s_k)^2$. At the corresponding fixed phase the ambient displacement from $C_{s_k}$ is bounded by that last integral, so each complete turn approaches the entire reference circle uniformly. Normalize phase to $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ for this unit-turn estimate; changing normalization introduces only one fixed constant and does not affect convergence. Thus each late turn uniformly approaches the full leaf $C_{s_k}$; Hausdorff convergence of those leaves to $\Gamma$ proves both inclusions in $\omega_Y^+(y)=\Gamma$. The orbit stays in the compact disk and cannot cross $\Gamma$, since $Y=X$ there and uniqueness applies. The proof uses only the fixed product, finite compactness, and the explicit locally finite band sum. The input field and modified field are only C¹. Existence, uniqueness, compact containment and finite-time continuity are supplied by [[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]], using its C¹ clause. The C² product makes W=Ψ_*∂s a C¹ field, so the existing band estimates and flat C¹ zero-extension apply without a C² generator. No θ-independent speed is needed.

items.title: Foliation components as mutual positive transverse-accessibility classes
items.statement: Let F be a C² cooriented codimension-one foliation on a smooth manifold M without boundary. Its foliation component containing a leaf A is the saturated subset $$\mathcal C_F(A)=\bigcup\{B:B\text{ is a leaf},\ A\succeq_F B\text{ and }B\succeq_F A\}.$$ The equivalence classes of leaves under mutual positive transverse accessibility partition the leaf set; their unions partition M into saturated subsets. This is Novikov’s connected component of the foliation. It is not defined as an ordinary connected component of M or M minus a leaf, and it differs from one-direction positive reach alone. A boundary leaf L of a distinct component means $L\cap\mathcal C_F(A)=\varnothing$ and $L\subseteq\partial_M\mathcal C_F(A)$, with boundary in the ambient topology. This definition does not assert that a component’s closure is a manifold with boundary.
items.strategy: [[lem-positive-transverse-accessibility-is-a-preorder]] makes mutual accessibility an equivalence relation. Apply [[def-equivalence-relation]] and [[lem-equivalence-classes-partition]] to the set of leaves: equal leaf classes give equal unions, distinct classes give disjoint unions because leaves themselves are disjoint, and every point belongs to the class of its leaf. Saturation is built into the union of full leaves. The geometric shape, openness of nontrivial classes and the compact-manifold/finitely-many-boundary-leaves theorem for their closures are separate source §1 obligations, not part of this definition.

references.title: S. P. Novikov, The Topology of Foliations, English translation by J. A. Zilber
references.locator: §1, Definition1.4 and Lemma1.1, printed p.2; mutual-accessibility component definition immediately following Lemma1.1

items.title: A null simple center frontier supplies the exact cancellation scalar
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. Let a maximal nested-circle basin in a generic characteristic disk have one simple homoclinic frontier through one saddle and precisely its center in the interior. If its leafwise rounded image is null, a fixed cap supplies a C² first integral on a full neighborhood of the closed lobe and saddle, equal to the transported cap section on a regular exterior collar. After choosing the transverse sign so the center is a minimum, its Euclidean negative gradient has precisely one saddle unstable half-trajectory entering the lobe and tending to the center; the other exits a regular local section. Thus all scalar, branch, collar and fixed-cap hypotheses of the conditional simple-lobe cancellation carrier hold.
items.strategy:
Null simple frontier gives the missing cancellation scalar

Let Ω be the nested-circle basin about p and let its frontier Γ be one simple homoclinic loop through q, with no other zero in its closed disk. Its source interior occupies one saddle quadrant: if it occupied three, the two unused characteristic separatrix half-rays would lie inside Ω, whereas every point of Ω other than p lies on a periodic orbit. Uniqueness excludes that possibility.

Suppose the rounded image of Γ is null in its leaf. Fix one leafwise cap. The ambient holonomy germ of Γ is therefore identity on both sides, since leafwise homotopic loops have equal holonomy and a null loop has identity holonomy. Cover q and the compact regular edge of Γ by finitely many boxes. In the q box use u=z∘f, with u(q)=0. Transport this coordinate along the edge by the transverse chart transitions. Identity holonomy makes the returned coordinate exactly u on a two-sided interval. Consequently the finitely many scalar expressions glue to a single C² first integral on an open neighborhood N of Γ, with du≠0 off q and the original nondegenerate saddle Hessian at q up to a nonzero factor.

Choose its sign so u<0 on the basin quadrant. On an inner periodic curve C contained in N, this scalar is a regular coordinate on the ordered period-annulus base. Extend it inward to the center by a strictly increasing C² coordinate on that base, matching u on a full collar of C and matching a positive affine change of the local center function near p. This extension is explicit: take two disjoint endpoint base collars, use the supplied C² period product to choose a scalar base coordinate on the compact interval between them, choose a positive C¹ derivative matching the prescribed endpoint derivatives, and adjust its integral by a positive bump to match the endpoint values. The center affine scale and offset are free, so the total value difference can first be chosen larger than the fixed endpoint-collar integrals. Integration gives the C² coordinate. All transitions are increasing C² diffeomorphisms. It extends the first integral over Ω, has precisely the minimum p, and preserves the first integral on N. In particular u(p)<u(q)=0. Take W to be Ω with a thin exterior regular neighborhood of Γ; it contains no other critical point.

For the *standard source Euclidean metric*, -∇u has two saddle unstable half-rays. Exactly one lies in the basin quadrant; the other lies in the opposite sign-negative quadrant outside Ω. The inside ray cannot leave Ω: u strictly decreases along it, while the whole frontier has value zero. Starting at any negative level it remains in a compact inner disk. If its limiting value were greater than u(p), a compact regular level band would have |∇u|≥m>0, contradicting d u/dτ=-|∇u|²≤-m². Hence its value tends to u(p). Any accumulation point then has value u(p), which occurs only at p, so the trajectory tends to p. The other ray is regular immediately after leaving a small saddle chart and crosses a short transverse exit section before reaching any other singularity. Thus the precise Euclidean-gradient hypothesis in the existing conditional cancellation item is genuinely supplied; an arbitrary characteristic vector field was never called a gradient.

The scalar just constructed and the cap-product section t_C may use different coordinates, but their differentials annihilate the same source line field on the connected regular outer collar. Their local increasing transition functions agree on overlaps by the same two-sided identity-return relation. Reparameterize u on that collar by this transition, then extend inward using the positive-derivative construction above. Near q use the corresponding increasing reparameterization of z∘f. The resulting scalar is exactly t_C on the old outer collar, not merely a first integral with the same level sets. The Euclidean-gradient branch conclusions are unchanged because a positive scalar reparameterization multiplies ∇u by a positive function.

items.title: A nested pinched center frontier gives a strict inner-disk search
items.statement: Suppose the frontier of a center basin is two simple homoclinic loops through the same saddle q, with one loop nested inside the other. Their inner bounded disk K occupies one saddle quadrant, contains a center, and does not contain the selected basin center. Searching from any center of K remains inside K. If another nested two-loop frontier occurs in that search, its inner disk K′ is properly contained in K and has strictly fewer interior saddles. This is a selection statement in the original source disk; it does not assign an essential boundary class to K.
items.strategy: The four half-branches at q alternate incoming and outgoing. A simple directed loop joins an adjacent incoming/outgoing pair. In the nested embedding the inner loop has its bounded side in one quadrant and the outer loop has its bounded side in three; their difference, the pinched basin, occupies the two remaining sectors. The one-quadrant index lemma gives a center inside K. The selected basin and K are disjoint, so that center differs from the selected center. The boundary of K is invariant. Uniqueness for the C¹ characteristic field prevents regular trajectories from crossing it; hence all nested periodic disks from a center in K remain there. Their frontier may reach its boundary circuit, but if it does then it is that one simple circuit, not a new nested pair. Any new nested pair therefore has a saddle r strictly inside K. Its inner disk K′ is contained in K and excludes r, while r was counted among the interior saddles of K. Thus s(K′)≤s(K)−1. The boundaries are source circuits; their image classes need not be essential and are not silently used as such.

items.title: A separated characteristic disk has a minimal nonidentity simple cycle
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. A relative generic characteristic disk with closed transverse boundary and distinct singular images in distinct ambient leaves has an inclusion-minimal simple regular or homoclinic characteristic cycle whose ambient holonomy germ is nonidentity. Its bounded source domain minimizes area among such cycles. This minimum-selection statement alone does not assert inward identity at a three-sector homoclinic cycle.
items.strategy:
New geometric nested-cycle bound closes original-disk minimum selection

This section supersedes §5's provisional stop. It uses the *new* geometric interface sent by the period-frontier author: decreasing periodic Jordan curves inherit a one-intersection property on every sufficiently short everywhere-transverse section. It does not assume the earlier unproved arbitrary-chain bound.

First take a trajectory entering the transverse disk boundary, outside the stable separatrices of the finitely many saddles. Its omega limit cannot contain a center: a sufficiently small invariant center circle cannot be crossed. The local generalized Poincaré–Bendixson argument gives a periodic orbit or finite saddle graph. Separation of singular ambient leaves reduces a connected graph to one saddle. The return word along the orbit's eventual graph itinerary is nonidentity: if it were identity on a full interval, the actual characteristic return on the section would be identity and sufficiently late iterates of the approaching orbit would instead be periodic. For two homoclinic edges the word factors into the two lobe words; if both were identity their composite would be identity. Thus there is a simple regular or homoclinic source cycle with nonidentity ambient holonomy.

Let A be the infimum of areas of bounded domains of all such simple cycles in the *unchanged* source disk. There are only finitely many singular simple cycles: each is a homoclinic orbit based at one of finitely many saddles, and each saddle has four half-branches. If one of these attains A, use it. Otherwise choose regular cycles with area tending to A, using AC_ω. Each bounded regular-cycle disk contains a center by the ordinary boundary-degree index count. There are finitely many centers; an infinite subsequence contains the same center p. Two characteristic circles containing p are disjoint and nested, because trajectories do not cross and their bounded Jordan domains intersect. Extract a decreasing subsequence: the areas converge to the infimum, so if no minimum is already attained, there are arbitrarily later strictly smaller areas. Call the resulting closed disks K_n and their circles C_n.

A fixed sufficiently small center neighborhood is contained in every K_n: a C_n cannot cross its invariant circles and cannot lie entirely inside that neighborhood, since the image of each such small circle is plaque-null and has identity ambient holonomy. Hence K=intersection K_n has nonempty interior and positive area.

Obtain a Hausdorff subsequence of C_n by finite rational square covers of the compact disk and a deterministic diagonal selection of the finitely many occupied cells at each mesh; this requires only the already declared AC_ω and compact Euclidean completeness. Its limit G is invariant under the characteristic C¹ flow by uniform dependence on initial points on compact time intervals. It is connected. Every short transverse section in a regular flow box meets each C_n at most once: all oriented crossings have the same sign, whereas Jordan entry/exit crossings must alternate. At a regular limit point, the flow-box projection of approaching points gives a unique approaching section intersection, and hence exactly one local regular arc of G. The nested inside sides converge to the inside side of that arc; this identifies G with ∂K at every regular point. At a saddle, the local first-integral levels and the four port sections give only the incident separatrix half-branches; no other regular arc can accumulate there without meeting one of those sections. Center charts are excluded as above. Thus G=∂K.

The limit has no separate regular periodic component unless it is that whole periodic orbit: such a component is locally open in G by its flow-box circle cover and closed by compactness, whereas G is connected. A regular edge cannot have an additional nonsingular limiting component because each regular limit point has only the one flow-box arc; equivalently the local PB proof applies using the inherited one-section-point property. Therefore each nonperiodic edge has saddle alpha/omega endpoints. There are finitely many saddle half-branches, so G is a finite graph. Internal chain transitivity also follows directly: approximate two points of G by points on the same C_n, follow that periodic orbit in finitely many flow-time segments, and project its points to G with uniform flow dependence. The terminal-SCC trapping argument from the period author then makes G strongly connected. Separation reduces it to one saddle, with one or two homoclinic edges.

Now trim each regular edge and place one short transverse section at its midpoint. For large n, C_n hits every such section at least once by Hausdorff convergence and the local flow-box projection, and at most once by the Jordan crossing argument. It therefore traverses each edge exactly once. The finitely many saddle ports leave only finitely many circuit itineraries; take a subsequence with one itinerary. Cover the trimmed edges by fixed finite ambient plaque chains. At each saddle, its small source neighborhood maps into a single ambient foliation box, so replace the passage there by a reference plaque path with its two port endpoints. Every actual passage has that same plaque transverse label. Thus all C_n have, after their specified transversal identifications, the holonomy germs of *one* return word H at parameters t_n tending to zero. This proves the geometric word bound rather than assuming it. If H were identity at zero on an interval, it would be identity at all sufficiently late t_n, contradicting the nonidentity of C_n. Therefore H is nonidentity at zero.

If G is a regular circle or a simple homoclinic loop, it is the required limiting nonidentity cycle. If it has two edges, at least one simple lobe has nonidentity word. Its entire bounded Jordan domain is contained in each K_n: its boundary lies in K_n, while the connected unbounded exterior of K_n is disjoint from that boundary and lies on its unbounded side. This argument does not assume the lobe's image is null. The limiting domain has area at most lim area(K_n)=A; the infimum definition gives area at least A, so it attains A. For this area inequality no measure-continuity theorem is needed: a bounded Jordan domain contained in every K_n has its area bounded by each area(K_n). Every strictly interior nonidentity simple-cycle domain would have strictly smaller area, since the two distinct boundaries leave a nonempty open source region between them. Thus this cycle is inclusion-minimal among the original source cycles. There is no modification of the disk in this proof.



Area means the published planar Lebesgue measure: the bounded open Jordan domains are Borel and have finite measure under ACω. Any strict domain difference used here contains an open box of positive volume; measure additivity and monotonicity give strict area inequality. No unproved measure continuity is used for the limiting comparison.

items.title: Closed defining forms have vanishing Godbillon-Vey class
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$ defined by a closed nowhere-vanishing $1$-form $\omega$ with $TF=\ker\omega$ (so that $\ker\omega$ is integrable by [[prop-closed-constant-rank-one-forms-define-integrable-hyperplane-fields]]). Then $\mathrm{GV}(F)=0$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$.
items.strategy: For a closed defining form take $\eta=0$: the identity $d\omega=0=0\wedge\omega$ holds and $\eta\wedge d\eta=0$, so the class defined in [[def-godbillon-vey-class]] is the class of the zero form. This applies in particular to the fibre foliations of bundles over $S^1$ defined by the pullback of a volume form on the circle. No choice principle is used.

references.locator: §3.1, printed p. 11

items.title: Godbillon-Vey invariance under smooth foliated concordance
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $F_0,F_1$ be smoothly foliated-concordant transversely oriented codimension-one foliations of $M$ ([[def-smooth-foliated-concordance]]). Then $\mathrm{GV}(F_0)=\mathrm{GV}(F_1)$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$.
items.strategy: Let $(G,\omega)$ be a concordance on $W=M\times[0,1]$ and choose $\eta$ with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, so that $[\eta\wedge d\eta]=\mathrm{GV}(G)\in H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(W;\mathbb R)$. By the restriction lemma, $i_j^{*}(\eta\wedge d\eta)=(i_j^{*}\eta)\wedge d(i_j^{*}\eta)$ represents $\mathrm{GV}(F_j)$, hence $i_j^{*}\mathrm{GV}(G)=\mathrm{GV}(F_j)$ under the pullback [[thm-pullback-induces-a-well-defined-map-on-de-rham-cohomology]]. The inclusions $i_0,i_1:M\to W$ are smoothly homotopic: the identity of $W$, read as the smooth family $H(x,s)=(x,s)$, restricts to $i_0$ and $i_1$ at the ends. By smooth homotopy invariance, $i_0^{*}=i_1^{*}$ on $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(W;\mathbb R)$, so $\mathrm{GV}(F_0)=i_0^{*}\mathrm{GV}(G)=i_1^{*}\mathrm{GV}(G)=\mathrm{GV}(F_1)$. All regularity is smooth; no choice principle is used.

items.title: The Godbillon-Vey class requires at least C-two regularity
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The Godbillon-Vey class is a secondary invariant of codimension-one foliations of class $C^2$ or better; no invariant of $C^1$ (or less regular) foliations is asserted on this page. The construction of the auxiliary form $\eta$ with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$ and the closedness of $\eta\wedge d\eta$ use one derivative of the defining form beyond $C^1$; for a $C^1$ foliation the fine invariant is the Godbillon measure, not the cohomological class $\mathrm{GV}(F)\in H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$ of [[def-godbillon-vey-class]].
items.strategy: Recorded as the regularity threshold of the classical theory: the cohomological definition is stated for $C^2$ foliations, while the $C^1$ theory is formulated through the Godbillon measure. This is a caveat, not a construction; nothing on this page uses it as a hypothesis.

items.title: Limit cycles of a leaf
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, $L$ a leaf, and $x\in L$. For a chosen side $j$ of $L$, let $N_j(L,x)\triangleleft \pi_1(L,x)$ be the subgroup of classes whose one-sided normal-fence holonomy germ is the identity. The quotient $P_j(L,x)=\pi_1(L,x)/N_j(L,x)$ is Novikov’s one-sided limit-cycle group. A class $[\alpha]$ is a **limit cycle on side $j$** precisely when its image in $P_j(L,x)$ is nonidentity, equivalently its one-sided holonomy germ is nonidentity. The two groups $P_+(L,x)$ and $P_-(L,x)$ record ordinary right and left limit cycles; they are distinct from the limitwise-nullhomotopy subgroup $\Pi^j_1(L,x)\subseteq N_j(L,x)$ defined below.
items.strategy: Novikov defines a right (respectively left) limit cycle by the failure of a normal fence to meet all sufficiently nearby leaves in closed curves; the classes for which every such intersection is closed form $N_j$, and the ordinary limit-cycle group is $P_j=\pi_1(L,x)/N_j$. In codimension one this is exactly nonidentity of the one-sided holonomy germ. Novikov’s notation for the separate subgroup $\Pi^j_1$ is reserved for classes in $N_j$ whose nearby displaced loops are null-homotopic; it must not be identified with $P_j$.

items.title: A compact leafwise cap transports nullity across a regular characteristic orbit
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $P$ be a regular closed characteristic orbit in a generic disk map, and suppose its based class is trivial in its ambient leaf $L$. Then the characteristic return map on a transverse section in the disk is the ambient foliation holonomy of $P$, hence is the identity germ. The adjacent characteristic period annuli therefore consist of closed prescribed level loops; every sufficiently close loop on either side is null-homotopic in its own leaf.
items.strategy: Because $P$ is regular, choose a small transverse section in the disk at a point of $P$. Along the regular orbit, foliated-chart transport on this section is exactly the first-return map of the characteristic line field: the orbit lies in one ambient leaf and the section maps transversely to $F$. Triviality of $[P]$ makes its holonomy germ the identity, so every sufficiently close point on the section returns to itself and the nearby characteristic trajectories close on each side. Choose one compact continuous leafwise nullhomotopy of $P$. The resulting actual level-loop trace is a transverse deformation of $P$; apply [[lem-nullhomotopy-persists-under-a-compact-transverse-deformation]] to transport that fixed disk map. Its boundary is the prescribed characteristic loop, so those loops themselves are null-homotopic. This argument is for regular orbits only; it does not identify holonomy with characteristic return across a saddle polycycle.
