items.title: A first-saddle lobe admits a collar-fixed center–saddle cancellation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth $3$-manifold and let $f:D^2\to M$ be a $C^2$ disk map with a regular outer collar. Suppose the characteristic foliation of $f$ has a compact embedded disk lobe $\Omega\Subset\operatorname{int}(D^2)$ whose regular leaves are the full nested circles about one nondegenerate center $p$. Suppose its frontier is one embedded piecewise-$C^2$ separatrix circuit $\Gamma$ with one nondegenerate saddle $q$ and otherwise regular arcs; there are no other characteristic critical points in a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}\cup\{q\}$. Let $u_0$ be the cooriented $C^2$ first integral on the full circle annulus, continued across the center/saddle block and its regular collar. For the standard Euclidean metric on the source disk, assume $-\nabla u_0$ has exactly one unstable half-trajectory from $q$ entering $\Omega$ with forward limit $p$, while its other unstable half-trajectory exits through a regular transverse section before any other singularity. Assume $f(\Gamma)$ lies in one ambient leaf $L$ and fix a leafwise smoothing collar from the saddle corner to a regular loop $\gamma\subset L$, together with one compact $C^2$ filling of $\gamma$ in $L$. After flattening the fixed collars, the leafwise cap has outer boundary exactly $f(\Gamma)$. Then one can choose a compact regular-neighborhood block $W\Subset\operatorname{int}(D^2)$ containing the lobe and saddle and construct a replacement map $f_{\mathrm{new}}:D^2\to M$ with the same outer boundary map, equal to the original map on an open collar of $\partial W$ and outside $W$, and with no characteristic critical points in $W$; all characteristic singularities outside $W$ are unchanged, so exactly one center and one saddle are removed. No homotopy from the original map on the interior of $W$ is asserted.
items.strategy:
The preferred route is the same-run Morse cancellation criterion, not the oversized cubic cutoff. The exact application target is a compact collared surface triad (the Morse slab) inside the regular-neighborhood block. Choose a regular intermediate value $v$ between the critical values and place the exit section below $v$ on the outgoing branch, so the second point of the saddle attaching sphere is present at level $v$ outside the center disk. Retain the full lobe circle at $v$ and this marked exit point in its regular exit tube. Complete the initially open exit interval by a regular product strip to an external circle, then continue that external circle as a product cylinder below and above the critical band. The normalized field $Z=\nabla u_0/|\nabla u_0|^2$ satisfies $du_0(Z)=1$ throughout each such regular collar, so no new critical point is introduced. This gives a compact annular triad with two full incoming/outgoing circle faces and exact face collars; round its corners in the regular product region, away from the selected trajectory and the cancellation support. The center disk is born at $p$, and the saddle one-handle joins it to the external component. Choose regular levels $a<v<b$ around the critical values of the minimum $p$ and saddle $q$, with no other critical point in the slab. At the intermediate level, the saddle attaching sphere is the two-point set $A_q\cong S^0$ of the two descending branches; the minimum belt sphere is the full circle $B_p\cong S^1$ bounding the disk component born at $p$. The branch tending to $p$ meets this circle at exactly one point. The other branch crosses the prescribed exit section below $v$, so its point at level $v$ is outside that disk and contributes no intersection. Since a point and a regular curve in the one-dimensional intermediate level meet transversely, $A_q\cap B_p$ is exactly one transverse point. Thus, once the compact slab and this level-set description have been locally constructed, [[prop-morse-cancellation-criterion-via-a-unique-connecting-orbit]] cancels the index-zero/index-one pair under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and [[lem-cancellation-modification-can-be-supported-in-a-trajectory-neighbourhood]] confines the modification to any chosen open neighborhood of the compactified connecting orbit and $p,q$, rel the two faces. The two-item edge is recorded against batch 3; its choice premise is inherited explicitly.

For the disk-map application, first form one fixed enlarged cap disk $\widehat W$ by gluing the specified leafwise filling to the plaque projection of f on a fixed collar crossing Γ, with the prescribed smoothing collar and a flattened open seam. The resulting C² map B into L agrees with f on the interior curve Γ. Apply [[lem-fixed-leafwise-cap-gives-a-joint-transverse-product-with-exact-collar]] on this fixed enlarged disk and obtain P on $\widehat W\times J$ before choosing the final outer collar. In the transported section coordinate, t_C=0 on Γ. By compactness of Γ and continuity, a sufficiently thin closed collar around Γ has actual section range S compactly contained in the fixed J. Choose the actual block W as Ω with a thinner exterior collar inside that region, keeping p,q and the compactified connecting arc in its interior. Its closed outer collar C0 then satisfies S=t_C(C0)⊂⊂J although the section on ∂W need not vanish. Choose S⊂⊂I⊂⊂J and restrict P to W×I. The factorization f(x)=P(x,t_C(x)) is exact on C0 and its interior; factorization of the original map on the cap interior is not required. Choose the cancellation support U around the compactified connecting arc and p,q with closure inside W and disjoint from C0. The auxiliary slab extension lies outside that support, so the supported scalar modification restricts back to the source block and remains equal to the original scalar on an open collar.

The scalar u0 is C². On a compact inner region, smooth compactly supported pieces by finite convolution: for |α|≤2, D^α(F*ρ_h)=(D^αF)*ρ_h and uniform continuity of D^αF gives convergence in C². In small convex critical neighborhoods, if H is the original invertible Hessian and σ its least singular value, keep D(grad u_s) within σ/2 of H throughout the interpolation; the integral mean-value formula gives |grad u_s(x)−grad u_s(y)|≥(σ/2)|x−y|. [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]] continues the unique critical zero, the nonzero boundary gradient prevents escape, and its Hessian inertia is unchanged. On the compact regular complement, a positive gradient minimum excludes new zeros. In the regular connecting band, the interpolants remain submersions and the C¹ time-dependent field Y_s=−(ubar−u0)grad(u_s)/|grad(u_s)|² transports their level components. [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution]] supplies local uniqueness; a compact buffer and |Y_s|≤||ubar−u0||∞/m keep the flow inside the band for 0≤s≤1. Choose an adapted descending field along a transported regular section from the saddle-facing ray to the minimum, route the other ray through the separate exit tube, and patch in regular charts with positive weights: du(X)<0 is preserved. This realizes one attaching point on the center circle and the other on the external circle, without assuming a parameter-dependent unstable-manifold theorem. Complete the exit tube by the auxiliary rectangle and product cylinder with matching scalar t-collars, apply the two batch3 suppliers there, and restrict the change supported in U back to W. Finally blend the cancelled smooth scalar vbar to u0 on a separate outer regular annulus: with X=grad u0/|grad u0|², choose the approximation so d vbar(X)>1/2 and sup|dρ(X)| ||vbar−u0||∞<1/4; then d((1−ρ)u0+ρ vbar)(X)>1/4. The result is C², has no new collar critical point and preserves the exact outer germ.

After the supported cancellation, let $K_v$ be the compact range of the replacement scalar on $W$. Choose a smooth strictly increasing map $\vartheta:\mathbb R\to I$ that is the identity on a neighborhood of the compact collar-value set $S$ and sends $K_v$ into $I$. Such a map is made by choosing a positive derivative on the two compact tails and adjusting its integrals below the endpoint margins of $I$. The identity on $S$ keeps the old collar exactly fixed, while $d(\vartheta\circ v)=\vartheta\prime(v)dv$ creates no characteristic critical point. Thus $P(x,\vartheta(v(x)))$ glues pointwise to the original disk map on the open collar. No relative homotopy of the original interior map is claimed.

This is a conditional local construction strategy under the explicit simple-lobe, exit, smoothing-collar and fixed-cap hypotheses. The compact-triad completion, regular-band smoothing adapter and fixed enlarged-cap/thinner-block range choice are spelled out in research/frontier-41-ha-dt-29-batch-23-local-center-saddle-carrier-completion.md. The complete local construction supplies the stated conditional interface; later item authoring must write out this strategy. Nothing here produces the simple lobe or fixed cap from an arbitrary characteristic disk, proves period-annulus recurrence, or closes Haefliger/Novikov selection. The cubic cutoff is not used.

Pointwise cap-product gluing is realized by the unique transverse-flow-root supplier, rather than by retaining each box's plaque coordinates independently. The new scalar supplier supplies all stated hypotheses when the lobe is selected by finite disk search; if needed reverse the transverse orientation for this conditional application so the center is a minimum. The underlying foliation and resulting map are unchanged by that orientation choice.

items.title: A center period annulus has an orbit or polycycle frontier
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a $3$-manifold, and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a disk map in the relative generic position of [[lem-characteristic-disk-map-can-be-put-in-generic-position-rel-boundary]]. The connected family of regular closed characteristic trajectories surrounding any center has a maximal period annulus. Its outer frontier is a regular closed orbit; or a finite connected strongly connected directed saddle-separatrix graph whose edges are nonconstant saddle-to-saddle trajectories and whose edges are covered by finitely many directed saddle polycycles; or, when the disk boundary is a leafwise characteristic orbit, that boundary orbit. Loops, repeated saddle vertices, shared edges, and parallel edges are allowed in the saddle graph and polycycles. When the disk boundary is transverse to $F$, the period annulus cannot meet it. The annulus parameter gives a $C^2$ transverse trace of the prescribed closed characteristic loops. The outer return holonomy is not assumed nontrivial.
items.strategy:
Choose a finite foliation-box cover of the compact image of h and a finite C² source partition of unity subordinate to its pullback. The local cooriented transverse covectors du_i differ by positive nonvanishing C¹ factors on overlaps. Their weighted sum β therefore has exactly the characteristic kernel and singularities, and is C¹. Equivalently β=h*ω if a global defining form ω has already been fixed. Choose an oriented source area form μ and define X by ι_Xμ=β. The local foliation transverse functions u=z∘h are C², and β=f du with nonzero C¹ f, so X is C¹ and its regular line foliation has the C² first-integral atlas used below. The given generic disk has finitely many centers and saddles, all interior, and a nonsingular boundary collar. Extend X as a C¹ field to an open neighborhood U of the compact source disk by [[lem-c1-planar-fields-on-a-closed-disk-extend-to-a-neighborhood]]. This is an extension of the field only.

Fix the specified center c. Let P_c be the set of all points on regular periodic X-orbits contained in int D whose bounded Jordan interiors contain c. A nonconstant periodic orbit is an embedded circle: choose its least positive period using a local flow box and compactness, and uniqueness rules out a repeated point before that period. Its time parametrization is C² since X is C¹. The center-level picture supplied by the generic-position lemma gives a punctured neighborhood of c consisting of such circles, so int P_c is nonempty. The flow preserves P_c and its interior. Let A be the connected component of int P_c containing that small center collar. Components of an open planar set are open (a small connected ball through any point belongs to its component), and A is flow-saturated because each orbit is connected. Two of its circles are disjoint by uniqueness and both contain c in their bounded interiors; Jordan separation therefore puts one compact circle strictly inside the bounded interior of the other. To spell out this familiar nesting use: one circle, being connected and disjoint from the other, is entirely in one of its two complementary components. If both circles lay in each other's exteriors, their bounded components would be disjoint: the bounded component of the first is connected, disjoint from the second circle, and contains points on its own collar on the same exterior side of the second; hence it lies in the second's exterior. This would contradict their common point c. Thus the circles in A are strictly nested. Orient them by X; their agreement or disagreement with boundary orientation is a locally constant sign on connected A and hence consistent.

The local and global construction in [[lem-c2-first-integral-period-annuli-have-c2-products]], with the explicit connected-open-set formulation recorded in this proposal, now proves that A is an annulus and gives a C² product Ψ:S¹×(0,1)→A increasing in the nesting order. Its hypotheses are exactly the C² atlas, compact circle leaves, nesting, consistent orientation, and connected openness just established. For clarity the crucial local return step is not an assumption of open periodic stability: a short everywhere-transverse interval in a first-integral box meets each global circle at most once, because every crossing has one fixed boundary-orientation sign, whereas entry and exit across a Jordan curve alternate. The finite cyclic plaque return therefore fixes every point of a sufficiently short section. The finite phase gluing and the ordered one-dimensional quotient then produce local and global products. A is maximal among connected open regular circle families continuing the chosen center collar, because any such extension is an open subset of P_c and hence lies in this same component. This proves existence and maximality without choosing a maximal chain or using Zorn. In product coordinates X=a(s,θ)∂θ with a positive C¹ function, using the product supplier's finite-regularity clause, not a C² flow of X.

Write C_s=Ψ(S¹×{s}), Ω_s for its bounded open Jordan component, and Ω=⋃_{0<s<1}Ω_s. All closed bounded domains lie in D: their exterior contains the connected complement of the source disk, so their bounded interiors cannot leave the source disk. For s<t the entire compact closed domain of C_s lies in Ω_t, and C_s⊂Ω_t. Put Γ=∂Ω in the plane. This is a nonempty compact subset of D, and it separates c from any specified point q outside D: c lies in a fixed Ω_s, q lies outside cl Ω, and every path between them has a first exit from Ω, on Γ. No connectedness or graph regularity of Γ is assumed at this stage.

Here is the complete Hausdorff exhaustion argument. For r∈(0,1) set T_r=cl(⋃_{s≥r}C_s), a nonempty compact subset of D. These sets decrease with r. Every C_s is in Ω, so their tail intersection K∞ is contained in cl Ω. If x∈Ω_t, a ball about x lies in Ω_t, and every C_s with s>t avoids that ball; hence K∞∩Ω=∅. Thus K∞⊂Γ. For any ε>0, if arbitrarily late C_s had points at distance ≥ε from Γ, the nested compact sets T_r∩{x∈D:dist(x,Γ)≥ε} would all be nonempty and have a common point, contrary to K∞⊂Γ. This proves sup_{x∈C_s}dist(x,Γ)→0. Conversely fix p∈Γ and ε>0. Choose x∈Ω∩B_{ε/2}(p) and t with x∈Ω_t. For s>t, x∈Ω_s while p∉Ω_s; along the segment from x to p, the boundary C_s is met, at a point within ε/2 of p. Cover compact Γ by finitely many balls B_{ε/2}(p_i), make these finitely many choices x_i,t_i, and take s>max t_i. Then every point of Γ is within ε of C_s. Consequently C_s→Γ in Hausdorff distance, and Γ⊂cl A. These are finite choices for each ε, not a chosen sequence of witnesses.

No center belongs to Γ. The original center c lies in the fixed open set Ω_t. For any other center d, take a sufficiently small saturated center disk V disjoint from c. Every regular orbit meeting V is a complete small level circle in V, by uniqueness, so it does not enclose c and cannot belong to A. The smaller center disk is therefore disjoint from cl A and from Γ. All equilibria on Γ are consequently among the finite nondegenerate saddles of the characteristic disk.

If ∂D is transverse, use a source boundary collar coordinate r≥0 measuring inward distance. Since β is nonzero on the boundary tangent, Xr is nonzero on ∂D. Its sign is constant along this connected compact circle, and continuity gives one δ>0 and k>0 with |Xr|≥k and that same sign throughout 0≤r≤δ. A periodic orbit in D cannot enter this collar: if Xr<0 its forward trajectory cannot leave the collar through r=δ and must exit D within time δ/k; if Xr>0 the same assertion holds in backward time. Hence A and its closure avoid a smaller boundary collar. In the leafwise-boundary case the nonsingular collar makes ∂D one regular periodic X-orbit. If Γ meets it, invariance obtained below includes that entire orbit in Γ, and the generalized PB alternatives force Γ to equal it: a regular boundary orbit cannot be a saddle-to-saddle trajectory. This verifies both boundary clauses without assuming a leafwise boundary collar is foliated by closed circles.

All hypotheses of [[lem-flat-drift-realizes-a-period-annulus-frontier-as-an-omega-limit]] have now been checked: compact disk, C¹ neighborhood field, C² nested leaf product, and compact Γ=∂Ω. It supplies a C¹ field Y on U (shrink U if needed) and a positive orbit with compact closure in D⊂⊂U and ω_Y(y)=Γ, with Y=X and DY=DX on Γ. In particular Γ is compact, connected and invariant; its regular Y-trajectories are X-trajectories because equality on invariant Γ and uniqueness identify them. Apply [[lem-local-generalized-poincare-bendixson-for-a-precompact-planar-orbit]]. A singleton equilibrium is impossible because Γ separates c and q, whereas the complement of one point in the plane is polygonally connected. If Γ has no equilibria, it is one regular periodic orbit. Otherwise every regular point is on a trajectory with saddle alpha- and omega-limits. The branch and terminal-component proof in [[lem-finite-saddle-omega-graph-is-strongly-connected]], corrected explicitly in this proposal, then proves that Γ is a finite embedded strongly connected directed saddle graph, covered by finitely many directed saddle polycycles. This applies also to loops, parallel edges and repeated vertices. It uses the four local characteristic branches at each saddle, not an assertion that the general PB theorem has finitely many connections.

Finally, for any fixed phase θ₀, s↦h(Ψ(θ₀,s)) is C² and transverse to F: its pulled-back characteristic covector is nonzero on ∂s because ∂s is transverse to ker β. These are precisely the prescribed closed characteristic loops C_s; their holonomy can be identity or nonidentity, and no holonomy conclusion is needed. The only countable selection here is the product supplier's ACω selection of a countable chart and gluing system. Compact-tail intersections, finite collar covers, the field extension, the explicit flat drift, and finite graph arguments require no AC or DC. This completes every clause of the stated frontier result.

items.title: An area-minimal three-sector cycle has identity inward holonomy
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. In a separated generic characteristic disk, let P be a simple homoclinic cycle with nonidentity full ambient holonomy whose bounded source domain minimizes area among all such simple regular or homoclinic cycles. If its bounded side occupies three saddle quadrants, the unused branches form an inner one-quadrant homoclinic loop Q with identity full holonomy. The actual inward source return along the pinched P-and-Q itinerary therefore equals the inward P-holonomy. This inward germ is identity, while the opposite-side germ is nonidentity.
items.strategy:
The three-sector port closes by the global area minimum

This is the root-requested precise local construction and supersedes §7's residual stop. The selected source cycle P minimizes the area of its bounded Jordan domain among *all* source simple cycles with nonidentity full ambient holonomy. Thus a nonidentity cycle with a smaller domain is impossible even when it shares the boundary saddle q. This stronger fact is essential.

Suppose the bounded side of the simple homoclinic P occupies three saddle quadrants. Let b be the unused unstable half-trajectory from q on this bounded side. Source uniqueness keeps b inside the bounded domain. Its closure is compact. A center cannot be its omega limit or belong to that limit: a small periodic center circle is invariant, and a trajectory cannot cross it. A singleton saddle r different from q is impossible, since it would make b a q-to-r connection, contradicting distinct singular ambient leaves. A periodic omega orbit lies strictly inside P. Its attracting return germ is nonidentity: an identity return on a neighborhood would close b into a periodic orbit, contradicting its alpha limit q. This gives a smaller nonidentity cycle, contradicting global minimal area.

For the remaining nonsingleton omega alternative, generalized PB and the finite branch argument give a finite connected saddle graph. Distinct singular leaves give only one saddle r. If r≠q, the graph cannot touch P: a regular touch would include the trajectory P and hence q, while a singular touch is q itself. It is therefore strictly inside P. The orbit approaching the graph follows a finite saddle-port itinerary, with an actual characteristic return given by the ambient edge word and single-box saddle passages. If this word were identity on a neighborhood, the approaching orbit would be periodic. Thus the word is nonidentity; if there are two homoclinic edges at r, at least one lobe word is nonidentity. That simple cycle is strictly inside P and again has smaller area.

It remains to exclude a nonsingleton omega graph at q. There are only four half-branches. A graph containing the unused unstable branch contains a regular point of b. The regular-edge clause of generalized PB says that such an omega-graph trajectory has a saddle as its forward endpoint. Applied to b itself it would force b to tend that saddle, making omega(b) a singleton rather than the proposed graph. Consequently a nonsingleton graph at q can contain only the used branches, and is P itself.

But omega(b)=P is incompatible with the three-sector incidence. Choose fixed small incoming and outgoing saddle port sections in C¹ Morse coordinates u=xy, so P uses one adjacent incoming/outgoing pair and its bounded side is the three-quadrant side. A sequence of b-points approaching a regular point of the incoming P branch flows to the incoming port by regular compact-edge transport. On the bounded side its small nonzero u-level enters the adjacent *interior* quadrant; the hyperbola passage exits at the unused unstable port. Its exit point tends the regular b-port point as u tends zero (on x=δ the second coordinate is u/δ). Since omega sets are closed and invariant under passage with these compact ports, that b-port point belongs omega(b). It does not lie on P, a contradiction. The divergent passage time at q is harmless: the exit times tend to infinity and the exit points converge, exactly the omega-limit criterion. No ambient/source holonomy identification is used in this exclusion.

Therefore b tends q along a stable half-branch. It cannot tend q along the used stable branch, because that regular branch already belongs to the trajectory P; uniqueness would identify b with P although their unstable half-branches differ. It must return along the unused stable branch. Hence the two unused branches form a homoclinic loop Q wholly inside the bounded P-domain. The bounded Q-domain lies in the bounded P-domain by Jordan separation: the connected unbounded complement of the latter is disjoint from Q and lies on its unbounded side. Q's bounded side is its one-quadrant side; its three-quadrant side would contain the exterior quadrant of P, which is impossible for a contained domain. Q has strictly smaller area than P, since the domains are distinct and their difference contains a nonempty open region. Global minimality therefore implies that Q's *full two-sided* ambient holonomy germ is identity. This conclusion uses no leafwise nullity of Q.

Trim the two loops at the four fixed saddle ports. In the pinched region between P and Q the source hyperbola pairing connects a P-port to a Q-port and then the other Q-port back to the remaining P-port. The regular edge maps are the fixed C² holonomy continuations. Each local saddle passage stays in one ambient plaque and has the identity transverse map in that q-box coordinate. Thus the actual characteristic return on a regular P-edge section on its bounded side has word

    H_P composed with H_Q or H_Q^{-1},

up to the one fixed transversal conjugacy and order convention. Since H_Q is the identity on a full interval, this source return equals H_P on its inward interval. This is the missing realized-return port. It was proved by constructing and eliminating the auxiliary loop, rather than by directly calling the inward ambient P-word a source return.

Suppose H_P were nonidentity inward. Pick a sufficiently small nonfixed parameter in an open nonfixed interval, and orient time so its return displacement is toward the pinched interior. The corresponding one-circuit characteristic segment through the P-and-Q edge strips is simple: a self-intersection would make it periodic before its nonfixed return. Close its two distinct section endpoints by the short transverse section interval. No other intersection occurs with that interval after shrinking the finite graph strips and the section: the realized first-return segment has no intermediate section hit. The resulting piecewise-regular Jordan curve lies strictly inside the bounded P-domain. On its characteristic part the field is tangent; on the short closing section it points into its bounded disk for the chosen time orientation. At the two joins, round inside arbitrarily small regular flow boxes using curves whose inward field component is nonnegative. Uniqueness/first-exit then gives a compact positively invariant source disk strictly inside P. This disk does not contain q: q lies on the boundary of the larger P-domain, while a Jordan curve in its interior has its whole bounded domain there.

Choose an entering trajectory in this trapping disk which is not a saddle stable separatrix for the chosen time orientation. There are finitely many separatrices and each has discrete crossing times on its real time domain, hence countably many section intersection points, so such a point exists in the open nonfixed section interval. Center limits are excluded by the invariant-circle argument. PB yields a periodic orbit or finite one-saddle graph strictly inside P. Its approaching-return word is nonidentity as above; in the graph case at least one simple lobe has nonidentity word. This gives a smaller-area nonidentity simple cycle, contradicting the selected global minimum. Therefore H_P is identity on the inward half-transversal. Its full germ was nonidentity, so it is nonidentity on the opposite side.

Combined with the regular-cycle and one-sector case from §6, this proves the full original-disk Haefliger minimum one-sided-cycle conclusion. Interior centers and saddles may remain; the false all-interior-trajectories-closed assertion is neither stated nor used. All selections remain finite or countable under AC_ω. The three-sector construction uses global area minimality, source saddle pairing, PB regular-edge endpoints, and the full identity germ of the smaller auxiliary Q; it never needs a cap for Q.


Area means the published planar Lebesgue measure: the bounded open Jordan domains are Borel and have finite measure under ACω. Any strict domain difference used here contains an open box of positive volume; measure additivity and monotonicity give strict area inequality. No unproved measure continuity is used for the limiting comparison.

items.title: Limitwise-nullhomotopy predicate on based loops
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, $L$ a leaf, $x\in L$, and $j$ one of its two sides. For a based loop $f:S^1\to L$ whose class belongs to $N_j(L,x)$, and for a chosen sufficiently short normal fence on side $j$, define the representative-level predicate $Q_j(f)$ to hold when every sufficiently small positive normal displacement $f_\epsilon$ is null-homotopic in its leaf. At this stage $Q_j$ is a predicate on a specified loop and fence; no representative-independence is part of this definition.
items.strategy: Novikov’s §3 condition is stated here first at the representative level: membership in $N_j$ makes the displaced curves closed, and $Q_j(f)$ records that they are null-homotopic for all sufficiently small positive normal parameters. The next lemma proves that this condition descends to based homotopy classes and is independent of the fence.

items.title: A finite characteristic circuit has C² regular port traces
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. For a finite regular-edge/saddle circuit and a chosen adjacent period annulus following its finite itinerary, all regular port sections may be parameterized by transported transverse first integrals with nonzero derivative. The regular edge strips and endpoint collars are jointly C² down to the frontier. The nearby periodic loops force the one-sided composite transverse return map of that itinerary to equal identity on an interval.
items.strategy:
Actual C² saddle ports and the correct rounding statement

The saddle port issue does not require parameterizing hyperbolas through their singular limit. Choose short regular transverse sections through the two branches of a chosen passage, away from q. In the target foliation box their scalar z∘f restricted to each section has nonzero derivative. The C² scalar-root theorem therefore gives the endpoints as C² functions of t, including t=0. Along each compact regular edge, finite first-integral boxes produce a jointly C² strip: choose its source tangent parameter in the regular kernel direction and solve z∘f=t for its transverse coordinate. On overlaps use the exact coordinate transitions, and keep common open parameter collars. All port derivatives transverse to the ambient foliation are nonzero.

For a finite circuit itinerary, its corresponding nearby periodic orbits force the *one-sided* composite transverse return map to be identity on an interval. This is stronger than a converging sequence of unrelated identity germs. Each passage is replaced in the target plaque by a C² joining path, with a jointly C² correction on the two regular port collars. Explicitly, if E(θ) is the endpoint joining path and Y_±(θ,t) the prescribed collar traces, set

    A(θ,t)=E(θ)+χ_-(θ)(Y_-(θ,t)-Y_-(θ,0))
                    +χ_+(θ)(Y_+(θ,t)-Y_+(θ,0)).

Choose the two cutoffs supported in disjoint larger collars. For small t this stays in a convex plaque disk, agrees exactly on the smaller open collars, and has z=z(t) with z'(t)≠0. The patch is leafwise homotopic to the original saddle passage rel ports by convex interpolation. The return identity closes the complete trace. Different saddle visits use the C² nonzero-derivative transverse transition z_j(t); no unjustified common numerical chart coordinate is assumed.

A leafwise immersed endpoint representative can be obtained, when needed, by first making small leafwise perturbations of *all* endpoint regular arcs and corner paths inside finitely many plaque disks. A compact interval path in a two-dimensional plaque can be replaced by a finite polygonal path with nonzero edges and rounded corners with nonzero velocity; choose the finitely many vertices so adjacent directed edges are not opposite, preserving common collars chosen for this replacement. Make the same modification to each positive-t strip by its plaque coordinates. It preserves the leafwise classes and its transverse parameter. Immersion at t=0 persists for sufficiently small t by compactness and C¹ continuity. Exact equality to the raw f-images on the original regular arcs is unnecessary and is not asserted.

The current rounding Statement should be repaired from “family of prescribed characteristic level loops” to “family leafwise freely homotopic, for each positive parameter, to the prescribed characteristic level loops, obtained by these tracked plaque replacements.” A hyperbola family in the saddle model xy=t has no jointly differentiable parametrization through the original saddle corner with the required endpoint regularity. The true class-preserving trace is exactly what the vanishing-cycle definition and cap persistence consume. This is a local correction of an overly literal auxiliary formulation; the main vanishing-cycle theorems are preserved.

items.title: Limitwise-nullhomotopy predicate descends to a normal subgroup
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The set of classes in $N_j(L,x)$ satisfying this predicate is a well-defined normal subgroup of $\pi_1(L,x)$. Thus every conjugate remains in the set.

items.title: Limitwise-nullhomotopy subgroup of a leaf
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, a leaf $L$, a base point $x\in L$, and a side $j$, define $\Pi^j_1(L,x)$ to be the set of classes $[\alpha]\in N_j(L,x)$ for which the predicate $Q_j(f)$ of [[def-limitwise-nullhomotopy-predicate-on-based-loops]] holds for a based representative $f$. By [[lem-limitwise-nullhomotopy-predicate-descends-to-a-normal-subgroup]], this is independent of the representative and fence and is a normal subgroup of $\pi_1(L,x)$. It is Novikov’s limitwise-nullhomotopy subgroup, distinct from the ordinary limit-cycle quotient $P_j$.
items.strategy: This packages the representative-level condition into a class-level subgroup only after the preceding lemma has proved that the predicate descends and has the subgroup property; thus the definition is justified without a circular appeal to well-definedness.

items.title: A generic null-transversal disk has a minimal one-sided cycle
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a $3$-manifold and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a disk map in the relative generic position of [[lem-characteristic-disk-map-can-be-put-in-generic-position-rel-boundary]], with boundary a closed transversal and with the images of its distinct characteristic singular points in distinct ambient leaves. Such separated data are obtainable rel the prescribed boundary collar by [[lem-characteristic-disk-singular-images-can-be-separated-into-distinct-leaves-rel-collar]]. Then there is a regular closed characteristic orbit or finite saddle polycycle $P$ in one ambient leaf $L$. Its holonomy germ is the identity on the inward half-transversal and nonidentity on the opposite side. The selection is inclusion-minimal among the source characteristic cycles with nonidentity holonomy and bounded simple-cycle domains. A vanishing-cycle application additionally requires a proved inward family and leafwise caps; a polycycle endpoint uses the separate construction in [[lem-saddle-polycycle-rounding-preserves-the-inward-transverse-family]] once its family hypotheses are supplied.
items.strategy: Choose the original-disk global area-minimum nonidentity cycle with the new minimum-selection supplier. For a regular cycle or one-sector bounded homoclinic lobe, nonidentity inward return gives an interior trapping curve and a smaller PB nonidentity witness, contradiction. For the three-sector bounded case apply the new area-minimal three-sector supplier: the unused branches either give a smaller attracting witness or close into inner Q; its smaller area forces full identity holonomy, so the actual inward P-and-Q return equals H_P. The same trapping contradiction gives inward identity. Full nonidentity then lies on the opposite side. Interior trajectories need not all be closed, and interior singularities are retained. The selected minimum is among original source cycles; no disk replacement is used.

items.statement: For a generic finite-double-point representative of a nonzero Π class, a sufficiently short one-field leaf-synchronized fence exists, compact leafwise sets separate from short nonzero flow displacements, and all level intersections use one fixed finite crossing word with a strictly decreasing subword-cut rank.
items.title: Fixed transverse fences and their finite crossing words
items.strategy:
Let K be the image of a compact intrinsic subset of a leaf, and V a smooth transverse vector field. There is η>0 such that φ_s(K)∩K is empty for 0<|s|<η. Cover K by finitely many intrinsic neighborhoods each contained in one plaque of a box. On pairs in the same such neighborhood, the transverse coordinate strictly changes along V, uniformly for short time. The complement of their union in K×K is compact and has no diagonal; continuity of the flow and the closed ambient diagonal give one short interval of inequality on that complement. Take the minimum. The same proof handles finitely many compact sets in distinct leaves by their disjoint intrinsic union.

Choose a smooth positive transverse field V near the compact loop by a finite positive combination of constant chart vectors. Cover the loop by finitely many boxes. In each box the V-flow lines are transverse, so the implicit function theorem identifies each nearby plaque with a graph over a small piece of the original loop using V-orbit projection. Successive plaque continuations starting at φ_t(f(0)) agree on overlaps by uniqueness of plaque transport. Finite subdivision gives a C² family F(u,t)=φ_{τ(u,t)}(f(u)) with τ(u,0)=0 and τ_t>0. The return time is the one-sided holonomy map on the base V-orbit. Because [f] is in N_j its germ is identity, so shrinking t gives F(0,t)=F(1,t) and a periodic time function τ. By the existing finite-chart fence-independence argument for Q_j, these closed loops are null on every positive sufficiently small level. This construction uses one fixed V throughout; arbitrary point tracks cannot be substituted in the next lemma. The regularity assertion uses C² box coordinates and the C² implicit function theorem for intersection with a V-orbit, not a C²-dependence claim for an arbitrary C¹ ODE.

Given a C² immersed generic loop f:S¹→L with N transverse double points and no triple points, choose its fixed-V fence F and shrink it so 0≤τ(u,t)<η/3, where η is the compact separation bound for K=f(S¹). If F(u,t)=F(v,t), flow uniqueness gives φ_{τ(u,t)-τ(v,t)}(f(u))=f(v). Separation forces τ(u,t)=τ(v,t), and then f(u)=f(v). Hence every double point at every level uses one of the same N fixed parameter pairs (u_i,v_i). The equality need not hold for all levels: it is used only where it actually holds. Shrink once more so regularity and nonparallel tangents at all possible double points persist. At a possible crossing the common flow time is the same; the tangential vectors are the original nonparallel vectors acted on by Dφ, with small transverse corrections imposed by leafwise tangency, so nonparallelness follows from compact C¹ control.

View f as a finite cyclic word of arcs by marking the 2N crossing preimages. A reduced word traverses some of these arcs, each at most once, with switches only at marked pairs. A selected crossing is a vertex visited twice; cutting there gives two cyclic subwords, each visiting that vertex only once. Neither new word can reintroduce a deleted arc or a second visit at a vertex already used for a switch. Define r(w) to be the number of original vertices visited twice by w, counting a switch vertex once (its two end representatives are one visit). Then each cut word has r≤r(w)−1. All possible non-endpoint collisions of any level of any reduced word are at vertices counted by r(w); absence of new intersections follows from the preceding flow-separation argument. This ranking is fixed by the original loop and is uniform over all lower parameters, even when closedness sets have many components.

items.title: Vanishing cycles of a codimension-one foliation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ transversely oriented codimension-one regular foliation. A **vanishing cycle** supported on a leaf $L_1$ is a jointly $C^2$ family of loops $\sigma_t:S^1\to M$, $t\in[0,1]$, such that: (i) each $\sigma_t$ lies in one leaf $L_t$ of $F$; (ii) $[\sigma_1]$ is nonzero in $\pi_1(L_1)$; (iii) $\sigma_t$ is null-homotopic in $L_t$ for every $t<1$; and (iv) for each $\theta\in S^1$, $t\mapsto\sigma_t(\theta)$ is transverse to $F$. The nearby loops in (iii) have trivial holonomy because they are null-homotopic, so a vanishing cycle is not an ordinary nontrivial-holonomy limit cycle. The supported class instead determines a nonzero element of the distinct subgroup $\Pi^j_1(L_1)$ on the side approached by the family, as proved in [[lem-a-vanishing-cycle-determines-a-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class]]. Here jointly $C^2$ means the trace map $S^1\times[0,1]\to M$ is $C^2$, with one-sided derivatives at the parameter endpoints; transversality requires its parameter derivative to have nonzero normal component. Smooth foliation data with a smooth trace are included as a special case.
items.strategy: This is the modern formulation of the vanishing-cycle family (Ranz, Definition 3.3), stated with transverse traces. A compactness argument near $t=1$ makes the trace annulus lie on one fixed side; the local finite-chart transport in [[lem-a-vanishing-cycle-determines-a-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class]] identifies it, up to leafwise homotopy, with normal displacements of $\sigma_1$. The nullhomotopy condition concerns $\Pi^j_1$, not the ordinary limit-cycle quotient $P_j$. Regularity is stated in the category of the foliation: $C^2$ chart changes and plaque projections produce $C^2$ loops and fences, which is sufficient for fundamental-group classes, finite chart transport and the nonzero transverse derivative. Ambient relative Whitney approximation is not used to claim a leaf-preserving $C^\infty$ trace for $C^2$ leaves. The C² regularity of specified plaque transports and compatible open-collar gluings is supplied by [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]; this does not assert existence of a saddle endpoint family.

items.statement: Finite transversal control: (i) an intrinsically noncompact leaf in compact M meets a C² positive closed immersed transversal; (ii) saturation of a transversal is open; (iii) a compact nearby leaf through a sufficiently small base parameter of a compact leaf is a one-sheeted collar graph, preserving essential transported loops.
items.title: Finite transversal control and compact collar graphs
items.strategy:
## Lemma B: a noncompact leaf meets a closed transversal

**Contract.** Assume ACω. Let F be a C² cooriented codimension-one foliation of a compact boundaryless smooth manifold M, and L an intrinsically noncompact leaf. Then there is a positively transverse C² immersed circle meeting L. No embeddedness or arbitrary-neighborhood clause is asserted.

**Proof, finite plaque detection.** Choose finitely many C² foliation boxes U_i with coordinates `(-2,2)^(n−1)×(-2,2)`, whose smaller open cores V_i, coordinates `(-1,1)^(n−1)×(-1,1)`, cover M. If L met each V_i in only finitely many U_i-plaques, then the finitely many corresponding compact plaque squares `[-1,1]^(n−1)×{r}` would be intrinsically compact subsets of L whose union contains L. Their union would equal L and make it compact. Hence one V_i meets infinitely many plaques of L. In particular, on its central vertical interval choose two distinct plaque points x=(0,r_x) and y=(0,r_y) of L with r_x<r_y.

**Proof, positive perturbation of the leaf path.** Connectedness of L and its local Euclidean charts give a finite piecewise C² leafwise path from y to x. Smooth its finitely many corners intrinsically in convex leaf charts, giving a C² path γ:[0,1]→L with γ(0)=y and γ(1)=x. It may have stationary points; regularity of γ is unnecessary. Such corner smoothing uses finite local interpolation, not manifold-valued Whitney approximation.

Construct ω and X near the compact path as described above, with smooth local flow φ. For small a≥0 put `v(s,a)=ω_(φ_a(γ(s)))(Dφ_a(γ′(s)))`. Since γ is leafwise, v(s,0)=0. The C¹ form, smooth flow and compact parameter domain imply uniform bounds `|v(s,a)|≤A a` and `ω(X)≥b>0` there. Indeed ∂_a v is continuous on a fixed compact neighborhood, so the ordinary mean-value estimate gives A.

Choose B>A/b and δ>0, and set `a(s)=δ(e^(Bs)−1)/B`. Then a(0)=0, a′=Ba+δ. For δ small, the path `γ_δ(s)=φ_(a(s))(γ(s))` is defined and C², and
`ω(γ_δ′) = v(s,a(s))+a′(s)ω(X) ≥ −Aa+b(Ba+δ)>0`.
Thus it is positively transverse, starting at y and ending at x_δ near x. In the original box, the transverse coordinate of x_δ is strictly above r_x, because X is positive there; make δ so small that it remains below r_y and the tangential coordinates stay in the core. The straight box-coordinate segment from x_δ to y lies in that core and has strictly increasing transverse coordinate. Its image under the C² chart inverse is positively transverse. Together these paths form a closed piecewise C² positive transverse curve.

**Proof, seam smoothing and intersection.** At each of its two joins, take a small foliation box and a parameter interval on which both one-sided transverse-coordinate derivatives have a common positive lower bound c. In chart coordinates mollify the continuous piecewise C² curve with a nonnegative smooth kernel. The mollified transverse derivative is an average of derivatives and remains ≥c. Blend the original curve and its mollification using a smooth cutoff equal to one near the join and zero outside the chosen interval. The added transverse derivative is the cutoff derivative times the difference of the transverse coordinates, which tends uniformly to zero with mollifier radius. Choose the radius so its absolute value is <c/2. The resulting chart curve is C², still positively transverse, and equals the old curve on open end collars; finite gluing gives a C² immersed circle.

At the join y, before smoothing the incoming transverse coordinate lies below r_y and the outgoing one lies above r_y. Keep those interval endpoints fixed. After smoothing the coordinate remains strictly increasing and crosses r_y by the intermediate value theorem. Its crossing point lies in the local plaque through y, hence in L. Therefore the smoothed closed transversal still meets L. ∎

This supplies a precise C²/ACω version of Novikov §1 Lemma1.2, printed p.3, without his “obvious approximation.” Batch22 already has `lem-a-non-closed-leaf-of-a-codimension-one-foliation-meets-a-closed-transversal`, but that statement concerns a leaf **not closed as an ambient subset**, outputs an embedded circle, and is in the smooth setting. It cannot silently be substituted for this intrinsic-noncompact/C² contract. The draft deliberately proves only the immersed closed-transversal conclusion needed here.



Saturation is open: join any leaf point to a crossing by a finite leafwise path. Finite box transport carries a small open transversal interval to one through that point, and the terminal union of plaques is an open neighborhood all of whose leaves meet the original transversal. Taking the union over eligible paths requires no selection of one path per point.

Use a finite foliation-box cover of L and a finite system of connecting paths and generating loops for π₁(L). Compactness permits shrinking the base transversal so all generator holonomy maps H_i and their inverses are defined on [0,ε], and the finitely many chart and connecting-path transports stay in a fixed tubular collar. All H_i are increasing and fix0. If B meets the base transversal at t, then H_i(t) and every defined iterate belong to B. If H_i(t)<t, its forward iterates form a strictly decreasing sequence in [0,t], converging to some fixed a≥0; if H_i(t)>t, use inverse iterates, again decreasing in [0,t]. The iterations remain defined in the common small domain. B is compact intrinsically, so its inclusion is an ambient embedding and closed; the limit transversal point belongs to B. A transverse interval meets an embedded leaf locally in an isolated point, contradicting the infinitely many distinct iterates converging to a. Hence H_i(t)=t for every generator.

For the graph conclusion, choose finitely many local plaques along a finite tree of connecting paths from the basepoint to the finite covering boxes. Continue the plaque through t along each tree path; this gives a finite collection of local sections over L, contained in the collar after the uniform shrink. On overlaps the difference of paths is a based loop. Express that loop in the finite generator system. Its holonomy at t fixes t because each generator and inverse does. Ensure the finitely many overlap path relations are valid on the chosen common transversal by finite subdivision of their compact homotopies into boxes, and shrink once more using only these finitely many relations. Thus the local sections agree on overlaps. They patch to a C² graph s_t:L→M, whose image is contained in the leaf B and is compact. Projection along the collar restricts to its inverse, so it is an embedding. Its image is open in B by the leafwise inverse function theorem and closed in B by intrinsic compactness; connectedness makes it all of B. The graph is therefore diffeomorphic to L. A transported loop projects to the original loop, so if it were null in B its projected nullhomotopy would null the original loop in L, proving essentiality.

The finite generator and finite-chart-tree system can be constructed from a finite cellulation of the compact surface L. This proof uses no finite-holonomy Reeb-stability theorem and asserts no product neighborhood for all nearby leaves. It only identifies the nearby leaves that are themselves compact.

items.statement: The maximal downward common interval of two closed/null cut words has closed endpoints and at least one essential factor unless their product initial loop is null.
items.title: Closed null fence words have essential lower endpoints
items.strategy: For a piecewise C² path following a fixed finite V-fence word, suppose at parameter r it is closed and has a compact nullhomotopy in its leaf. Finite subdivision of that compact cap into foliation boxes transports the cap over a uniform two-sided interval around r. On each boundary segment its transported path equals the prescribed word by uniqueness of plaque transport from the same initial V-orbit. In particular the ending point equals the initial point, since the cap boundary closes, and the word remains null. Thus its closed-and-null parameter set U is relatively open. Its closed parameter set E is closed because both endpoint tracks are continuous and M is Hausdorff. This does not assert U is closed. At a lower endpoint a of a component (a,r] of U, endpoint continuity makes the word closed; if the word were null at a, the same finite cap argument would extend U below a. Hence the word is essential at a (unless the component already includes the initial parameter).

items.title: A vanishing cycle determines a nonzero limitwise-nullhomotopy class
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation and let $(\sigma_t)_{0\le t\le1}$ be a vanishing cycle supported on $L_1$. For the side $j$ approached by the transverse trace annulus, the class $[\sigma_1]$ is a nonzero element of $\Pi^j_1(L_1,x)$, where $x=\sigma_1(1)$. In particular its one-sided holonomy germ is the identity, so this conclusion does not say that $[\sigma_1]$ is an ordinary limit cycle.
items.strategy: Since $S^1\times[0,1]$ is compact and each point-track is transverse, near $t=1$ the trace annulus is a one-sided transverse fence for $\sigma_1$. Cover the compact annulus by finitely many foliation charts and subdivide it into rectangles contained in single charts. In each rectangle, plaque coordinates identify its upper loop with the normal displacement of its lower loop up to a path in a plaque; the identifications agree on shared edges, giving a leafwise homotopy from the trace loop $\sigma_t$ to the normal displacement of $\sigma_1$ for every sufficiently small parameter. The former loop is closed and null-homotopic on its leaf by the vanishing-cycle hypotheses. Hence the displaced loop is closed, which makes the one-sided holonomy germ of $[\sigma_1]$ identity, and is null-homotopic, which puts $[\sigma_1]$ in $\Pi^j_1(L_1,x)$. Its class is nonzero by condition (ii) of the definition. The subgroup membership and choice-independence follow from [[lem-limitwise-nullhomotopy-predicate-descends-to-a-normal-subgroup]]. The C² regularity of specified plaque transports and compatible open-collar gluings is supplied by [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]; this does not assert existence of a saddle endpoint family.

items.statement: For the present closed connected smooth three-manifold with C² cooriented foliation, one compact sphere leaf forces every leaf to be a compact sphere. Consequently a nonzero Π leaf excludes every spherical leaf and every sphere universal-cover alternative.
items.title: Spherical stability at C² and countable-choice strength
items.strategy:
Local spherical stability is finite: cover a compact sphere by finitely many foliation boxes, choose finitely many connecting paths and finite overlap relations. Every based loop is contractible, so finite compact homotopy transport makes all these overlap transports identity on one common short transversal. They patch to a compact plaque graph for every sufficiently small transverse parameter, giving a saturated product sphere neighborhood. Therefore the union S of spherical leaves is nonempty, open and saturated.

The rational homology of the compact smooth ambient M is finite-dimensional without full AC. Choose a smooth metric by finite chart bumps. Local exponential-map IFT and the positive quadratic Hessian of squared distance, with uniform finite-chart bounds after shrinking, provide sufficiently small strongly convex balls with unique short minimizing geodesics. Take the collection of ALL such small balls; it covers M, and compactness selects finitely many. Shrink their uniform radius below the finite injectivity bound, so any nonempty finite intersection is geodesically convex: its two points have one common short geodesic, contained in each ball. Each intersection contracts to one of its points along these geodesics. Mayer–Vietoris, inducting on the finite number of cover sets and then on their finite intersection covers, shows that every H_k(M;Q) is finite-dimensional. This uses no choice of balls at every point and no unproved full-AC finite-CW theorem.

Let x∈closure(S), with leaf A. If A were intrinsically noncompact, for every finite collection of spherical leaves B₁,…,B_n construct a positive closed transversal through A avoiding that collection. This is the intrinsic-noncompact transversal construction with finite compact barriers: refine a finite ambient box cover so each selected compact embedded B_i has only its finitely many local plaques; an infinite-plaque A-box has infinitely many A plaques in one of the finitely many transverse intervals cut by these B_i plaques. Choose two there, join them by a finite path in A, positively perturb that path in the complement of the compact B_i union, and close by a positive vertical segment inside the same interval. Finite smoothing preserves the avoidance and positivity. Saturation of the resulting transversal is open and contains A, hence contains x and some spherical leaf B arbitrarily near x. This new B meets the transversal, while every chosen B_i misses it.

Oriented transverse intersection gives [B] outside the rational span of [B_i]: all intersections with B have one strict sign, whereas all intersections with B_i are absent. This is the finite compact intersection clause: subdivide a finite bounding chain into transverse chart pieces, and cancel paired internal faces to see a closed transversal has zero algebraic pairing with any rational boundary; therefore the nonzero intersection detects nonzero quotient homology. C² leaves suffice for this finite local perturbation and orientation count. Applying this to a finite basis of the span of ALL spherical-leaf classes contradicts the finite-dimensional H₂(M;Q). Thus A is compact.

Now apply the compact-nearby-leaf graph lemma to compact A. Spherical leaves B arbitrarily close through the chosen base transversal are compact, so their finite generator holonomies fix that parameter, and they are one-sheeted compact graphs over A. Hence A is diffeomorphic to B=S². This proves closure(S)⊂S without the false assertion that a connected saturated Hausdorff limit is one leaf. S is open, closed, nonempty, so connectedness gives S=M. All sphere-leaf fundamental groups are trivial, and therefore all Π groups are zero. Finally a compact simply connected oriented surface cover is a sphere by the finite surface normal form; its covered oriented leaf is also sphere (finite covering of a compact simply connected sphere has no nontrivial free orientation-preserving deck group, or use the finite Euler covering count). Thus the sphere-cover alternative is excluded in the nonzeroΠ application.

For completeness all leaves also meet a positive closed transversal when S=M. Their finite product neighborhoods are saturated, and any two distinct compact leaves have disjoint sufficiently small such neighborhoods; thus the quotient is Hausdorff. It is a compact connected cooriented1-manifold without boundary, covered by finitely many interval charts, so elementary finite interval gluing identifies it with a circle. These product charts make M a sphere bundle over that circle. Lift its one circuit to a product over [0,1] with endpoint monodromy f. A finite C² path in the connected sphere fiber from x to f^{-1}(x), constant on end collars, gives a section whose endpoint gluing agrees; its projection travels positively once around the circle, so it is a positive closed transversal. This finite construction supplies the no-transversal contradiction if spherical leaves are invoked without a separate nonzeroΠ assumption. For a compact simply connected oriented covering surface, compact-to-Hausdorff and discrete fibers give a finite cover of its leaf. Lift a finite base triangulation to count χ(cover)=dχ(leaf). The cover has χ=2; orientable finite normal forms give χ(leaf)=2−2g, so2=d(2−2g) forces g=0 and d=1. Thus a sphere universal cover means an actual sphere leaf, without a finite-group plane-action theorem.

Here is the local convex-ball input of the finite good-cover argument. The geodesic equation of the chosen smooth metric is a smooth finite-dimensional ODE. Its C² solution dependence and the inverse theorem give a local shooting inverse near (p,0). Differentiating a geodesic variation proves Gauss orthogonality: the radial tangent pairs to zero with variations of its unit initial direction, since the derivative of that pairing is one half the derivative of the constant speed squared. Hence radial distance in the exponential chart is actual minimizing distance there. In normal coordinates Hess(½d(p,·)²) equals the metric at p; on a smaller chart it stays positive definite. Uniform local ODE and shooting bounds ensure that the short geodesic between two sufficiently nearby points stays in a larger such chart. Along it this squared-distance function is convex, so endpoints in a small ball force the whole geodesic into that ball. Finitely many smaller charts covering compact M give one positive size bound. Taking all admissible smaller balls and a finite subcover uses finite compactness. Balls with radii below the bound have the same unique short geodesic between common points, so all their finite intersections are convex and contractible. No global metric-completeness, full-choice good-cover theorem or triangulation theorem is invoked.

items.statement: From a nonzero Π^j class represented by a generic finite-crossing loop, at every sufficiently small upper height one obtains after at most N subword cuts an essential lower loop with a coherent genuinely closed/null right family whose lifts are simple at EVERY positive parameter.
items.title: Finite compatible reduction of an arbitrary Π fence
items.strategy:
Begin with an essential loop at parameter a₀=0 and a closed/null family on (0,b], represented by the full cyclic word w₀. If every positive level has a simple lift to its leaf universal cover, stop. Otherwise choose one positive r≤b at which the lift has a selfintersection. The corresponding marked pair cuts the word into two loops c_t,d_t. At r both are closed and null: each is the projection of a closed subpath of the closed lifted loop, and the universal cover is simply connected. By finite compact-cap persistence both are closed/null on a neighborhood of r. Let (a,r] be the maximal common downward interval on which both are closed/null, relative to the current fence interval [a₀,r]. At a both loops are closed by continuity. If a>a₀ and both were null there, compact-cap persistence for both would extend the interval below a, contradiction. If a=a₀ and both were null, their product would make the current initial essential loop null, contradiction. Thus at least one factor is essential at a. Choose it, retain only the family on [a,r], and rebase and rescale. The new initial leaf need not be the old one; the family stays on the same chosen transverse side and every positive displacement is genuinely closed and null. The rank of its cyclic word is strictly smaller by the preceding lemma. Repeat only when an actual positive-level lift is nonsimple. There are at most N such operations. At termination ALL positive lifts are simple, since otherwise another rank-decreasing operation would be possible. The initial parameter belongs to [0,b), so choosing b arbitrarily small makes the reduced essential initial leaf arbitrarily close to L. No cut is projected below its common closed/null interval, and no claim about closedness of nullness is used.

The result is the finite reduction and simple lifted boundary part of Novikov Lemma7.2. Obtaining regular disk fillings from those simple lifts additionally uses the oriented simply connected surface/Jordan-disk supplier (sphere alternative included); the reduction does not identify a changing universal cover with ℝ². The source's sphere exclusion and coherent disk continuation are separate next steps.

At termination the finitely many switched corners can be rounded jointly before making regular cap charts. Choose small target plaque boxes at the switch vertices, disjoint from every other retained zero-level arc except the two adjacent half-arcs. The fixed finite crossing word has only one visit at each switch, so such boxes exist; compactness keeps all other positive arcs outside them after one shrink. Replace each corner by a C² regular joining arc and transport this replacement by the prescribed transverse plaque label. It is homotopic relative its two port collars and preserves nullness and essentiality. It creates no lifted collision, because the replacement is embedded in its small plaque box and there is no other retained arc there. Normalize the rounded zero representative back to one fixed-V fence by unique transverse roots and finite homotopy invariance of Π. The transported corner patches agree with that normalization in plaque coordinates; hence all sufficiently small positive lifted boundaries remain simple. This supplies genuinely C² boundary circles for the subsequent cap bundle, rather than tacitly using a corner as a smooth boundary.

items.statement: If a leaf L of a compact cooriented C² foliation meets no closed transversal, its strict positive accessible set N has compact C² manifold closure W with finitely many compact boundary leaves, including L, and positive normals point inward everywhere on ∂W.
items.title: A no-transversal leaf bounds a finite inward accessibility region
items.strategy:
Let N consist of endpoints of actual positive transverse paths beginning on L. Finite box endpoint perturbations and finite leafwise path transport make N open and saturated. It excludes L, because a positive path from L to L can be closed by the finite endpoint-alignment and positive smoothing construction to give a forbidden closed transversal. Short positive segments at every point of L show L⊂closure(N), hence L⊂∂N.

In a cooriented box, membership in the saturated set N depends only on the transverse coordinate z. If z∈N and z<z′ in that box, append the positive vertical segment to reach z′, so z′∈N. Consequently the transverse-coordinate membership set is an open upward interval: empty, all, or (a,upper). Around each boundary point it has exactly the latter form. Therefore ∂N is locally one whole plaque and closure(N) is locally the positive half-box. The boundary height is constant within its plaque box, so these are C² manifold-with-boundary charts for W=closure(N). Compactness of M gives compact W and a finite boundary box cover. Each boundary box contains just one boundary plaque; hence only finitely many boundary leaves occur, since distinct leaves have disjoint plaques.

Each boundary leaf C avoids closed transversals. Otherwise the saturation of a closed positive transversal through C is open and contains C; because C⊂closure(N), this saturation meets N. Thus some reachable leaf D also meets that same transversal. Following its positive orientation from a D-crossing to a C-crossing (going once around if needed) makes C reachable from D and hence from L. This contradicts C⊂∂N and C∩N empty. The intrinsic-noncompact-leaf transversal lemma then makes every boundary leaf compact. Equivalently, local one-plaque boundary charts and their finite compact plaque cores give a finite intrinsic compact covering. The positive normal direction points into N at every boundary point by the upward interval description. This is the strict accessible REGION of L; it is not automatically a mutual-accessibility class or the Π-side Reeb component.

items.title: The first essential loop in a transverse family is a vanishing cycle
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $H_t:S^1\to M$, $0\le t\le1$, be a jointly $C^2$ family whose loops lie in leaves and whose point tracks are transverse to a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation. If $H_0$ is null-homotopic in its leaf and $H_1$ is nontrivial in its leaf, there is a parameter $t_*\in(0,1]$ such that $H_t$ is null-homotopic for every $t<t_*$ and $H_{t_*}$ is nontrivial. After reparametrization, $(H_t)_{0\le t\le t_*}$ is a vanishing cycle and its endpoint determines a nonzero class in the limitwise-nullhomotopy subgroup on the approached side.
items.strategy: Let $S$ be the set of $s$ for which every $H_t$, $0\le t\le s$, is null-homotopic in its leaf. It contains a positive interval: $H_0$ has a compact nullhomotopy and [[lem-nullhomotopy-persists-under-a-compact-transverse-deformation]] transports it to nearby loops. Let $t_*=\sup S$. For every $t<t_*$, the definition of supremum gives an $s\in S$ with $s>t$, hence $H_t$ is null-homotopic. If $t_*<1$ and $H_{t_*}$ were null, the same compact-disk persistence lemma would make it null on a right-hand interval, contradicting the supremum; if $t_*=1$, nontriviality is the hypothesis on $H_1$. Thus $H_{t_*}$ is essential, and the restricted family is a vanishing cycle by definition. [[lem-a-vanishing-cycle-determines-a-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class]] then proves membership in $\Pi^j_1$ on the approached side. The opposite side holonomy, when supplied by the polycycle lemma, is not used for this membership. The C² regularity of specified plaque transports and compatible open-collar gluings is supplied by [[lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity]]; this does not assert existence of a saddle endpoint family.

items.statement: With the finite plane-bundle Euler boundary-sum carrier and oriented compact-surface normal forms, every no-closed-transversal leaf of the present closed oriented cooriented three-manifold foliation is a torus.
items.title: A no-transversal Π leaf is a torus
items.strategy:
Construct W and its finitely many compact boundary leaves C_i by the preceding local geometric proof. The oriented plane bundle TF extends over W and restricts on each C_i to TC_i. The ambient orientation and positive coorientation give TF its orientation. Since the positive normals point inward on every C_i, the boundary orientation of W is the same negative of this leaf orientation on every component. The finite tangent zero-count/inward-boundary-sum lemma constructs a generic rank2 section over W with oriented1-dimensional zero set and gives directly 0=−Σ_i χ(C_i). Its finite surface index count is V−E+F. No general Thom existence, 3D finite CW construction or unproved e_fin comparison is needed.

No C_i is a sphere. A compact spherical leaf would invoke the supplied C² global spherical stability theorem and force every leaf spherical, making L spherical and met by a closed transversal (or the whole foliation a sphere fibration), contrary to L’s no-transversal property and its nonzero Π class in the application. By the supplied finite oriented compact-surface normal form, all remaining C_i have χ(C_i)≤0. Their finite sum is0, so each χ(C_i)=0 and each is diffeomorphic to T². Since L is one of these boundary leaves, the ORIGINAL L is a torus. This obtains torus identification without first assuming that the Π-side accessibility class has sole boundary L. It does not assert that W itself is a solid torus.

items.statement: For a fixed-V fence with every positive loop null and simple in its leaf universal cover, and with the sphere-cover alternative excluded, the canonical based Jordan caps form a Hausdorff C² disk bundle over (0,b]. Its evaluation admits coherent regular C² cap development with V-orbit tracks over all positive parameters. If its zero loop is essential, at least one material point has infinite normal clock.
items.title: Canonical Jordan cap development and an infinite normal clock
items.strategy:
For t>0 choose the universal cover of its leaf based at the fence basepoint, and lift the entire null loop from that point. Its lift is simple. The surface-Jordan disk supplier gives the unique compact disk region Δ_t bounded by this lift; uniqueness uses that the universal cover is not a sphere. The sphere alternative is excluded by the separately supplied compact spherical-leaf global stability carrier: such a leaf forces the foliation to have only spherical leaves, whereas the initial loop is essential. Include the based coverpoint, not only its projected image, in Δ_t. Define E as the disjoint union of these Δ_t, with projection π to t.

At a fixed r>0 transport the compact cap over a small two-sided interval using finitely many foliation boxes and fixed-V roots. This yields a regular cap at every nearby t, with exactly the prescribed boundary word by transport uniqueness. Lift it from the prescribed basepoint to the universal cover of its leaf. A regular lifted disk map with simple boundary is a diffeomorphism onto the unique Jordan region: it is a local diffeomorphism; its degree across the boundary is ±1, and all local degrees have the same sign, so every point inside has exactly one preimage and every point outside none. The degree count follows by finite triangulation of the compact parameter disk and cancellation of internal oriented edges, so does not require a global uniformization theorem. Therefore the transported caps identify D²×J_r with E over J_r. If two such charts overlap, both identify each fiber with exactly the same based Jordan region. Their transition map is the inverse of one regular leafwise parametrization composed with the other. Locally this inverse is C² by the plaque inverse function theorem; uniqueness of the based lift fixes which local branch is used. Cover the compact common disk fiber by finitely many such branches to obtain a C² transition on a smaller overlap. The transition maps satisfy the cocycle identity because they identify actual based coverpoints, not arbitrarily chosen parametrizations.

These charts define a locally trivial Hausdorff C² disk bundle. For different base parameters disjoint base intervals separate points. For points in one fiber, one common product chart separates them by disjoint disk neighborhoods. Thus E is Hausdorff. Its projection is proper over compact parameter bands: shrink a finite cover of a compact band K by trivializing intervals to finitely many closed compact sets K_i inside those intervals; π^{-1}(K_i) is K_i×D² and compact, and their finite union is π^{-1}(K). The evaluation e:E→M is C² and a local diffeomorphism in the interior, because it has two independent plaque directions and one transverse direction. It may have multiple sheets; E retains their based coverpoints.

Lift the one fixed ambient field V through these local inverse branches, giving a C¹ field W on E. On overlaps the branches agree by the identified coverpoints, so W is globally defined. Along ∂E it is tangent to ∂E because the boundary fence tracks are V-orbits. Its π-component has one strict sign. After choosing that sign positive, normalize to W/(dπ(W)), so its base parameter has derivative1. On a compact positive band properness gives a compact total space, a positive minimum for dπ(W), and bounded local fields. The usual finite-chart ODE extension argument therefore transports the entire compact reference disk across the whole band; no interior solution can escape through the boundary because W is tangent there. Exhausting the positive interval by compact bands and using uniqueness gives coherent disk transport from the reference fiber at b to every t>0. Locally this transport is C²: a point is evaluated along a smooth V-flow from a C² cap chart, and the hitting time of a prescribed nearby plaque is the unique root of a C² scalar equation with nonzero derivative. The C² implicit function theorem gives the joint root and cap map. This uses the special transverse-root construction, not a false generic assertion that a C¹ vector field has a C² flow. The resulting evaluation G:D²×(0,b]→M is regular, has the specified boundary fence, and its point tracks follow V-orbits with possibly parameter-dependent speed.

Choose a C¹ defining form ω for the cooriented foliation and a smooth positive transverse field V on compact M, with ω(V)≥c>0. Such data are built by finite chart bumps. Let Φ be its smooth complete ambient flow and B=G_b the compact reference cap. Since D_xG_t is tangent to the foliation, differentiation gives 0=ω(DΦ_{−τ}D_xB)−ω(V)D_xτ, hence |D_xτ|≤C(T) whenever 0≤τ≤T. Indeed DΦ_s and DB are uniformly bounded for |s|≤T on the compact reference domain and compact M, and the denominator is ≥c. This is a bound in the fixed Euclidean disk domain, not an unsupported uniform leaf metric assertion.

If τ₀(x)=lim_{t↓0}τ(x,t) is finite, choose T>τ₀(x)+2δ with δ>0. For y joined to x inside D² by a path of length less than δ/C(T), τ(y,t) cannot reach T: at its first crossing of T along the path, the derivative bound up to that crossing would give T−τ(x,t)<δ, contrary to τ(x,t)≤τ₀(x)<T−2δ. Thus a fixed neighborhood of x has all clocks uniformly bounded by T. The same derivative bound gives local uniform Lipschitz control and makes τ₀ locally continuous wherever all clocks are finite in that neighborhood.

Suppose every clock is finite. The preceding neighborhoods cover compact D², so a finite subcover yields one global bound T for all x and t. The derivative formula then gives global equicontinuity. The monotone pointwise limits τ₀ are continuous and convergence is uniform: take a finite sufficiently fine disk net, obtain uniform convergence at its finitely many points, and use the common Lipschitz bound to control the remaining points. Therefore G_t converges uniformly to the continuous map G₀(x)=Φ_{−τ₀(x)}B(x).

This limit is intrinsically leafwise without a differentiability assumption. Around any x choose a small connected disk patch whose G₀ image lies in one foliation box; uniform convergence puts its G_t images in that box for small t. Each such G_t patch has constant transverse box coordinate, because it is connected and leafwise tangent. Passing to the limit gives constant transverse coordinate on the G₀ patch. Thus G₀ locally maps continuously into one plaque. Connectedness of D² makes all patches belong to one leaf, and its boundary is γ in the original leaf, so this leaf is the original one. Hence G₀ is a continuous intrinsic leafwise null cap for γ, contradicting essentiality. Some clock is therefore infinite. Only continuity of finite-clock limits is used; no unproved C² endpoint map or derivative convergence is invoked.
