items.title: Tautness is equivalent to the absence of dead-end components
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a compact manifold $M$. Then $F$ is taut if and only if $F$ has no dead-end component ([[def-dead-end-component]]). Moreover, if $N$ is a dead-end component, then $\partial N$ is a finite disjoint union of compact leaves and, when $M$ is a closed oriented $3$-manifold, every boundary leaf is a torus.
items.strategy: (A dead end implies not taut.) Let $N$ be a dead-end component and $\gamma$ a closed transversal. The function $s\mapsto\langle\gamma'(s),\eta_{\gamma(s)}\rangle$ along $\gamma$, where $\eta$ is a co-orienting vector field, is continuous and nowhere zero by transversality. Since $\gamma$ meets every leaf, it meets $N$; let $s_1$ be a first and $s_2$ a last parameter with $\gamma(s)\in N$. At the first entry the pairing is nonzero; replacing $\eta$ by $-\eta$ makes it positive, and by the intermediate value theorem and nowhere vanishing it is again positive at the last exit, so $\eta$ points outwards along the boundary leaf through $\gamma(s_2)$, contradicting 'inwards everywhere'. Hence no closed transversal exists and $F$ is not taut. (No dead end implies taut.) If $F$ is not taut, some leaf $L$ admits no closed transversal, and its accessible manifold $N_L$ is proper. Goodman's argument shows that $\overline{N_L}$ is a compact saturated submanifold with boundary a finite union of compact leaves lying on the positive side of each boundary leaf, hence a dead-end component: if a boundary leaf were noncompact it would meet a closed transversal by [[lem-a-non-closed-leaf-of-a-codimension-one-foliation-meets-a-closed-transversal]]; compactness of $M$ limits the boundary leaves to finitely many; and $N_L$ lies on the positive side of each of them by construction. (Boundary structure.) The inward co-orienting field on the compact manifold $\overline{N_L}$ gives $\chi(\overline{N_L})=0$ by Poincare-Hopf; gluing $\overline{N_L}$ to itself along $\partial N_L$ gives $\chi(\partial N_L)=0$. A boundary leaf of positive Euler characteristic would be a sphere or projective plane, and [[thm-local-reeb-stability]] then produces a double cover foliated by spheres, making $F$ taut, a contradiction; hence all boundary leaves have Euler characteristic zero, so in the oriented three-dimensional case they are tori. This is Ranz, Lemma 2.5 and Propositions 2.7-2.8, with Calegari, Lemma 4.28; only the standing countable choice is used.

items.title: Center-frontier selection and cancellation have a finite rank
items.statement: Assume AC_ω and the exact maximal-center-frontier contract. On a separated generic characteristic disk with transverse boundary or regular essential leafwise boundary, finite inner-source-disk search either finds a C² vanishing-cycle trace or selects a null simple one-center/one-saddle frontier whose exact collar-fixed cancellation reduces the full-disk saddle count by one. Iteration terminates in a vanishing cycle; its rank is (total saddles, interior saddles of the current invariant search disk).
items.strategy:
Finite selection and full disk theorem

Use the earlier disk-closure draft's three geometric additions: one-quadrant disk index count, strict inner-disk search for a nested two-loop frontier, and finite rank. Their role is now upgraded: each null simple endpoint supplies all ports of §2, rather than leaving the global scalar as an assumption.

The period-frontier interface yields the frontier of the maximal center annulus. Distinct singular ambient leaves prevent a connected characteristic frontier from containing different saddle vertices. A one-saddle graph has at most two homoclinic edges. The basin is an increasing union of its bounded periodic disks, hence a whole bounded complementary component of that graph. A side-by-side two-loop graph has separate bounded components, so one center basin has only one lobe as its frontier. A nested pair has a one-quadrant inner bounded disk K containing a center, by the inward boundary-degree calculation. Search from a center in K regardless of the two image lobe classes. Its trajectories cannot cross the invariant boundary. Any further nested pair has its saddle strictly inside K; its inner disk K' excludes that saddle and therefore has strictly fewer interior saddles. If a later frontier reaches ∂K it is that simple circuit. This is source topology and uses no inherited essential boundary class.

For a selected maximal annulus, near-center loops are null in a plaque. If any regular loop is essential, the first-essential-parameter lemma gives a vanishing cycle using the C² period trace. Otherwise all regular loops are null. An essential simple saddle endpoint gives a vanishing cycle using §3. A null simple endpoint gives one fixed cap and §2 cancellation. A null regular endpoint has trivial two-sided ambient holonomy; a regular source neighborhood then has a closed-orbit band across the endpoint, contradicting maximality. An essential regular endpoint gives the same first-essential trace. An outer transverse boundary cannot be the limit of periodic circles in its regular transverse collar. A regular leafwise boundary is the prescribed essential endpoint. An isolated outer center is impossible in a disk: a small punctured center neighborhood is foliated by circles, so joining this cap to the original center cap and intervening product annulus would form an open and closed compact surface without boundary inside the connected source disk. Equivalently their regular annulus has a circle at each end which is filled on opposite sides, producing a compact boundaryless two-dimensional submanifold of the interior disk; an inclusion is open locally, so compactness makes it closed, a contradiction.

Rank is (S,s(K)), lexicographically, where S is the total saddle count in the current full disk. Source descent lowers s(K). Null simple cancellation lowers S exactly by one, leaves the original outer collar fixed, and removes no other zero. Re-separate the finitely many remaining singular images rel that collar. At S=0 there is still a center by c-s=1, and the preceding regular/boundary alternatives yield an essential endpoint. Thus the full disk theorem follows in finitely many cancellations. Every regular annulus extension is absorbed into the *one maximal family* supplied by the frontier interface; no artificial iteration over ever smaller regular bands occurs.

Both wrappers now have short complete routes: an ambiently null closed transversal spans a relative C² characteristic disk, so apply the transverse-boundary disk alternative; a nonzero element of ker[π₁(L)→π₁(M)] is represented by a C² leaf loop spanning an ambient C² disk, so apply the essential-leafwise-boundary alternative. Neither ambient spanning disk is a leafwise cap.

items.statement: On the original compact torus leaf, a nonzero Π^j class has a primitive embedded representative with the same Π^j property; its sufficiently short fixed-flow fence is an embedded annulus and each positive boundary bounds an actual embedded disk in its leaf.
items.title: A torus Π class has a primitive embedded Π root
items.strategy:
Identify π₁(L)=Z² through the supplied torus normal form. Write the nonzero class α=mβ with m≥1 and β=(p,q) primitive, gcd(|p|,|q|)=1. The straight segment in R² from0 to(p,q) projects to an embedded torus loop g: if two interior parameter values had equal projections, their difference times(p,q) would be an integer pair, and Bezout’s identity would make that difference an integer, impossible between0 and1. Compact based homotopy transport identifies the original α fence loops with the m-fold loop of the g fence.

Let h be g’s increasing one-sided holonomy. Since α has identity one-sided holonomy, h^m(t)=t for every sufficiently small positive t. An increasing map has no nontrivial finite orbit: if h(t)>t then its successive iterates strictly increase, while if h(t)<t they strictly decrease. Thus h(t)=t, and the short displaced loops g_t close. Their m-fold loops are null by the transported compact homotopy and α’s Π property. Oriented-surface fundamental groups are torsion-free, so [g_t]^m=1 implies [g_t]=1. The original β is nonzero, giving a genuine embedded Π cycle on the same original leaf and chosen side.

Use the one fixed transverse flow to construct g’s fence F(u,t)=Φ_{τ(u,t)}g(u), with τ_t>0. Short compact-leafwise separation for g(S¹) gives injectivity of the FULL annulus: if F(u,t)=F(v,s), flow uniqueness gives Φ_{τ(u,t)−τ(v,s)}g(u)=g(v), so separation forces equality of times and of g(u),g(v). Embeddedness of g yields u=v, and strict τ_t yields t=s. Compact-to-Hausdorff then makes the fence an embedding. In particular every g_t is an embedded null curve in its actual leaf. The supplied surface-Jordan disk lemma in the leaf, rather than only in its universal cover, gives an actual embedded disk bounded by g_t. The spherical-leaf alternative is excluded as before, ensuring the selected disk is unique. This is the legitimate stronger input for the embedded Reeb construction, not a deduction of ambient cap embedding from the earlier simple universal-cover caps.

items.statement: Let G:D²×[a,b]→M be a C² immersed disk sweep, transverse in the time direction with one constant sign. Suppose an interior subdisk U⊂D² at the b-base is identified to the whole a-base by a diffeomorphism h:D²→U satisfying G(y,a)=G(h(y),b), with their leafwise tangent maps agreeing under h. On the quotient X, the induced map is locally open at every interior seam point; its compact image has boundary contained in the image of ∂X. No global injectivity is required.
items.title: Paired cap sweeps are locally open across their seams
items.strategy:
At a seam point choose a small leafwise plaque chart around its common image. The a-base and b-base maps have invertible leafwise differentials, so after shrinking each has a plaque inverse branch and its nearby time slices are graphs over that plaque patch. The differential in the time direction has the same nonzero transverse sign on both sheets. The piece of the cylinder adjoining the a-base has parameter t>a, whereas the piece adjoining the b-base has t<b. Therefore their transverse graph coordinates occupy opposite sides of the common base plaque, with uniform nonzero first derivative after shrinking. Each half supplies a local half-neighborhood of that plaque; their union supplies a full neighborhood. The leafwise identification h pairs the base inverse branches, so this is precisely a neighborhood of the seam point in X. Away from the seams, G is an ordinary local diffeomorphism by its two leafwise directions and transverse time direction. Thus every interior point of X has image locally open. Because X is compact and M Hausdorff, the image f(X) is closed. If z∈f(X) is not in f(∂X), each preimage is interior and any one gives a neighborhood of z contained in f(X); hence z is not a boundary point. Therefore ∂f(X)⊂f(∂X). This argument allows multiple image sheets and does not substitute immersion for an embedding.

On the unglued b-base annulus D²\U, the available cylinder side is t<b; if G_t is negatively transverse, that is the positive transverse side. Hence at each regular annulus point the positive transverse direction points inward to the locally occupied image side. A no-exit argument must separately control the lateral fence and possible multiple boundary sheets; the present lemma proves seam openness and image-boundary containment only.

items.statement: Let γ be an essential original loop and γ_t its short fixed-flow null fence boundaries. Every Jordan lifted disk cap of γ_t has projected image disjoint from γ and from one fixed intrinsic neighborhood of γ in its original leaf.
items.title: Jordan lifted caps avoid the original essential loop
items.strategy:
First split cases. If the reduced original leaf A is compact, shrink its positive fence using compact separation for K=A, so its positive boundaries and entire cap leaves are distinct from A. Every cap then misses the ENTIRE A, and uniform neighborhood avoidance is automatic. If A is noncompact, its torsion-free group follows from the compact-subspace-with-nonempty-boundary/free-word argument in the finite surface adapter. In that case use the following deck proof. Short fixed-flow separation for K=γ(S¹) makes every boundary γ_t disjoint from γ. If a projected disk met γ, its leaf would be the original leaf L. Lift the crossing to the disk in the universal cover of L. The lift of γ through it stays in the disk, because it cannot cross the disk boundary (its projection is disjoint from γ_t). The next lift of γ, starting at its endpoint, also stays in the disk; inductively the whole orbit under the nonidentity deck element α represented by γ lies in the compact lifted disk. Proper discontinuity of the deck action permits only finitely many orbit points in a compact set. Thus α has finite order, contrary to torsion-freeness of the oriented surface group. Hence the projected cap misses γ.

Choose a relatively compact intrinsic neighborhood S of γ in L and a smaller connected-near-γ neighborhood S′ with closure contained in S, so every point of S′ can be joined to γ by a path in S (finite leaf charts suffice). Compact flow separation for closure(S), not merely for γ, ensures every short γ_t avoids S. If a projected cap on L met S′, lift a path in S from that point to γ starting inside the lifted disk. It cannot leave the disk: crossing its boundary would project to an intersection of γ_t with S. Its endpoint therefore lies inside the disk and projects to γ, contradicting the first part. Thus all these cap images avoid S′ uniformly. Other-leaf caps are automatically disjoint from S′. This proof corrects the source’s unsupported uniform intrinsic-distance assertion by applying compact separation to an enlarged intrinsic compact neighborhood.

items.title: A Reeb component obstructs tautness
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ containing a Reeb component $R$ ([[def-reeb-component-in-a-cooriented-three-manifold-foliation]]). Then $F$ is not taut; equivalently, every taut foliation is Reebless.
items.strategy: Let $L_0=\partial R$ be the boundary torus leaf. The interior of $R$ lies on one side of $L_0$, and every interior leaf of $R$ accumulates on $L_0$ from that side; choosing the co-orientation to point into $R$, the accessible manifold $N_{L_0}$ does not meet the complementary side of $L_0$: a transverse curve crossing from $L_0$ into the interior of $R$ is trapped by the accumulating plane leaves and cannot leave $R$. In the model of [[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]] this is the monotonicity of $t-u(r)$ along a transversal, and it is transported to $R$ by the foliated homeomorphism of the definition. Hence $N_{L_0}\subsetneq M$, so the accessible-manifold criterion inside the proof of [[lem-a-foliation-is-taut-if-and-only-if-it-has-no-dead-end-component]] shows that $F$ is not taut. This is Ranz, Corollary 2.13(i), together with Goodman's accessible-manifold proposition; the same trapping computation shows directly that no closed transversal meets $L_0$.

items.title: A transverse volume-preserving flow forces tautness
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$, and let $X$ be a smooth vector field transverse to $F$ whose flow preserves a volume form $\mu$ on $M$, i.e. $L_X\mu=0$. Then $F$ is taut. (The flow of $X$ is complete because $M$ is compact.)
items.strategy: Suppose $F$ is not taut and let $N$ be a dead-end component, which exists by [[lem-a-foliation-is-taut-if-and-only-if-it-has-no-dead-end-component]]. Choose a co-orienting vector field pointing inwards along $\partial N$. A transverse flow with this co-orientation maps $N$ properly into itself: an integral curve starting in $N$ cannot cross $\partial N$ outwards without violating the inward co-orientation. Hence $\phi_t(N)\subseteq N$ with $\phi_t(N)\neq N$ for $t>0$, while $\mu(\phi_t(N))=\mu(N)$ by $L_X\mu=0$ and $\mu(N)<\infty$ because $N$ is compact; the proper inclusion leaves positive measure in $N\setminus\phi_t(N)$, a contradiction. This is Ranz, Lemma 2.10, and the converse of the flow criterion in Calegari, Theorem 4.29; completeness of the flow on the compact manifold is [[cor-every-smooth-vector-field-on-a-compact-manifold-is-complete]]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: A closed two-form positive on the leaves forces tautness and calibrates
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed oriented $3$-manifold, let $F$ be a co-oriented codimension-one foliation of $M$ (oriented by the rule that the leaf orientation followed by the co-orientation is the orientation of $M$), and let $\theta$ be a closed $2$-form on $M$ positive on $TF$: $\theta_p(v,w)>0$ for every positively oriented basis $(v,w)$ of $T_pF$. Then $F$ is taut. Moreover, with respect to the Riemannian metric for which $\theta$ has comass one and the transverse direction is orthogonal to the leaves, $\theta$ is a calibration and every leaf is a minimal surface (Rummler-Sullivan).
items.strategy: Suppose $F$ is not taut and let $N$ be a dead-end component; by [[lem-a-foliation-is-taut-if-and-only-if-it-has-no-dead-end-component]] the closure $\overline N$ is a compact oriented $3$-manifold with boundary a finite union of compact leaves $L_i$, and the co-orientation points inwards along every $L_i$. Stokes gives $\sum_i\pm\int_{L_i}\theta=\int_{\overline N}d\theta=0$. Each boundary leaf carries the orientation induced from the co-orientation and the orientation of $M$; because the co-orientation points inwards on every boundary component, all signs in the sum coincide, so $\int_{L_i}\theta$ has the same sign for all $i$, and each integral is nonzero because $\theta|_{L_i}$ is a positive area form on the compact leaf $L_i$. Hence the sum cannot vanish, a contradiction; so no dead-end component exists and $F$ is taut. (Calibration.) For the given closed form $\theta$, choose on each leaf the smooth metric whose oriented area form is $\theta|_{TF}$; choose a smooth metric on the transverse line bundle and make the splitting orthogonal. Then $\theta$ has comass one and restricts to the leafwise area form, so it calibrates every leaf and the leaves are minimal. The existence of a closed positive form from tautness is the separate Rummler-Sullivan existence direction (Calegari, Theorem 4.31; Ranz, Proposition 2.3); it does not follow by declaring an arbitrary leafwise area form closed. No choice principle beyond the standing countable choice is used.

items.title: A characteristic disk with essential boundary data produces a vanishing cycle
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a $3$-manifold, and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a disk map in relative generic position. Suppose either (a) $h|_{\partial D^2}$ is a closed transversal, or (b) $h(\partial D^2)$ is a loop in one leaf and represents a nonzero class of that leaf. Then $F$ admits a vanishing cycle.
items.strategy:
Finite selection and full disk theorem

Use the earlier disk-closure draft's three geometric additions: one-quadrant disk index count, strict inner-disk search for a nested two-loop frontier, and finite rank. Their role is now upgraded: each null simple endpoint supplies all ports of §2, rather than leaving the global scalar as an assumption.

The period-frontier interface yields the frontier of the maximal center annulus. Distinct singular ambient leaves prevent a connected characteristic frontier from containing different saddle vertices. A one-saddle graph has at most two homoclinic edges. The basin is an increasing union of its bounded periodic disks, hence a whole bounded complementary component of that graph. A side-by-side two-loop graph has separate bounded components, so one center basin has only one lobe as its frontier. A nested pair has a one-quadrant inner bounded disk K containing a center, by the inward boundary-degree calculation. Search from a center in K regardless of the two image lobe classes. Its trajectories cannot cross the invariant boundary. Any further nested pair has its saddle strictly inside K; its inner disk K' excludes that saddle and therefore has strictly fewer interior saddles. If a later frontier reaches ∂K it is that simple circuit. This is source topology and uses no inherited essential boundary class.

For a selected maximal annulus, near-center loops are null in a plaque. If any regular loop is essential, the first-essential-parameter lemma gives a vanishing cycle using the C² period trace. Otherwise all regular loops are null. An essential simple saddle endpoint gives a vanishing cycle using §3. A null simple endpoint gives one fixed cap and §2 cancellation. A null regular endpoint has trivial two-sided ambient holonomy; a regular source neighborhood then has a closed-orbit band across the endpoint, contradicting maximality. An essential regular endpoint gives the same first-essential trace. An outer transverse boundary cannot be the limit of periodic circles in its regular transverse collar. A regular leafwise boundary is the prescribed essential endpoint. An isolated outer center is impossible in a disk: a small punctured center neighborhood is foliated by circles, so joining this cap to the original center cap and intervening product annulus would form an open and closed compact surface without boundary inside the connected source disk. Equivalently their regular annulus has a circle at each end which is filled on opposite sides, producing a compact boundaryless two-dimensional submanifold of the interior disk; an inclusion is open locally, so compactness makes it closed, a contradiction.

Rank is (S,s(K)), lexicographically, where S is the total saddle count in the current full disk. Source descent lowers s(K). Null simple cancellation lowers S exactly by one, leaves the original outer collar fixed, and removes no other zero. Re-separate the finitely many remaining singular images rel that collar. At S=0 there is still a center by c-s=1, and the preceding regular/boundary alternatives yield an essential endpoint. Thus the full disk theorem follows in finitely many cancellations. Every regular annulus extension is absorbed into the *one maximal family* supplied by the frontier interface; no artificial iteration over ever smaller regular bands occurs.

Both wrappers now have short complete routes: an ambiently null closed transversal spans a relative C² characteristic disk, so apply the transverse-boundary disk alternative; a nonzero element of ker[π₁(L)→π₁(M)] is represented by a C² leaf loop spanning an ambient C² disk, so apply the essential-leafwise-boundary alternative. Neither ambient spanning disk is a leafwise cap.

items.statement: On the original Π torus, choose its primitive Π meridian β and a complementary longitude λ. Its one-sided longitude holonomy can be chosen strictly contracting. The collar longitude annuli grow the actual meridian caps, and their iterates exhaust each nearby leaf as a plane with limit set exactly the original torus. The limit set means ambient limits of sequences escaping every intrinsic compact subset of the leaf, equivalently the intersection of closures of tails of a cofinal compact exhaustion.
items.title: A contracting longitude exhausts the nearby plane leaves
items.strategy:
The meridian β has identity one-sided holonomy. Let H be the increasing longitude holonomy on a common small transversal. If H(t)=t at any sufficiently small positive t, β and λ both fix t, and the finite-generator graph lemma produces a compact one-sheeted nearby leaf. Its meridian is essential by collar projection, contradicting the Π meridian’s displaced nullness. Therefore H has no positive fixed point on one small connected interval. Replace λ by its inverse if necessary so 0<H(t)<t. Its iterates decrease to0, since their limit would otherwise be a positive fixed point.

Finite plaque transport over a cut fundamental polygon of the torus gives the actual collar suspension: β identifies the meridian edges without a transverse change and λ identifies the longitude edges by H. This construction uses finitely many compact chart relations, all valid after one common shrink. For each t the longitude circuit, thickened by the meridian coordinate, gives an embedded leafwise annulus A_t from β_t to β_H(t); its base projection travels once over the complementary torus annulus. Two disjoint embedded null circles in a nonspherical oriented leaf joined by an annulus have nested Jordan disks, and their disk difference is that annulus. Otherwise the two disks and annulus would form an open-and-closed sphere leaf. The nesting direction is locally constant in t by compact cap transport and the disjoint boundary circles. It cannot be shrinking: if D_H(t)⊂D_t, iteration would place every β_H^n(t) inside the compact D_t, but these circles approach the original torus, which is disjoint from D_t; the positive ambient distance of these two compact sets gives a contradiction. Hence D_H(t)=D_t∪A_t for every small t.

The union of increasing D_H^n(t) is the ENTIRE nearby leaf. Given any point of that leaf, join it to a point in D_t by a compact intrinsic path. Its ambient image is compact and disjoint from the original compact torus, hence has positive distance from it. Late boundary circles β_H^n(t) lie arbitrarily close to the torus and avoid that path. Starting inside the late disk, the path cannot leave it without crossing its boundary, so its endpoint belongs to the disk. An increasing union of disks with each compactly inside the next is a plane: choose successive disk/annulus homeomorphisms to concentric disks of radii n and glue them; the exact differences A_H^n(t) provide the required annuli. These annuli lie in collar heights tending uniformly to0. They therefore have no limit points away from the original torus; every point of that torus is approached, because their meridian/longitude base projections cover the entire torus. The compact initial disk contributes no intrinsic end-limit points. Thus the leaf limit set is exactly the original torus.

This limit-set convention is independent of the chosen exhaustion: any intrinsic compact subset is contained in a sufficiently late disk because those disks form an increasing open cover, and compactness selects finitely many whose maximum contains it. Thus the disk exhaustion is cofinal among intrinsic compact sets. Intersection of closed exhaustion tails and the escaping-sequence definition agree in the compact metric ambient space by choosing one point from each shrinking rational neighborhood and tail, using ACω. The annular tails approach L uniformly, while their torus base projections cover it, proving exactly L for that convention.

items.statement: Suppose the cap family has an infinite negative-transverse center trajectory q(s), synchronized parameters t(s)↓0, and the preceding fixed-neighborhood avoidance. Then after adjusting recurrence times there is one leaf B and one fixed plaque patch in B whose lifts lie in the interiors of all sufficiently late caps.
items.title: Infinite cap tracks give actual common-plaque recurrence
items.strategy:
Compactness of M and countable choice give an accumulation point z of q(s) for s→∞. Choose a small box around z where the transverse derivative of the fixed negative flow has a uniform nonzero bound. If q(s_n)→z, adjust each s_n by a time tending to0 so q(s_n) lies on the central plaque through z: solve the strictly monotone transverse-coordinate equation by the intermediate value theorem. The infinite trajectory permits both small time directions once s_n is large. These adjusted points all lie in the same leaf B.

The accumulation point z cannot lie on γ. Otherwise choose the box in the intrinsic neighborhood S′ of the original leaf provided by the avoidance lemma. The same small time adjustment places q(s_n) on its central original-leaf plaque inside S′, contradicting that q(s_n) is in the interior of a cap. Thus z∉γ(S¹). A fixed smaller box about z has closure disjoint from γ, and every late boundary γ_{t(s_n)} avoids that box by uniform convergence to γ. Each adjusted cap-center is interior to its Jordan lifted disk. In the lifted central plaque rectangle containing that center, disk-interior membership cannot change along a path without crossing the disk boundary. Since the entire projected rectangle is boundary-free and connected, it lies inside the lifted disk. Shrink to a fixed smaller rectangle around z and take n sufficiently large that the adjusted center belongs to it. This gives one common intrinsic plaque patch in B, with its lift based at a fixed point of that patch in every cap. The argument concerns actual central-plaque hits, rather than replacing ambient convergence by an assertion that the convergent points already share a leaf.

items.title: Reeblessness and tautness are not equivalent without extra hypotheses
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Tautness implies Reeblessness ([[lem-a-reeb-component-obstructs-tautness]]), but the converse fails without extra hypotheses. A Reebless foliation need not be taut: Ranz's Corollary 2.13(ii) exhibits the product of two juxtaposed bidimensional Reeb components with $S^1$, a Reebless foliation with two dead-end components, hence not taut (that example lives on a noncompact $3$-manifold); by [[lem-a-foliation-is-taut-if-and-only-if-it-has-no-dead-end-component]] a Reebless foliation is taut once it has no dead-end component, and Calegari records that Reebless plus atoroidal implies taut, so the missing hypothesis is not a definitional triviality. Likewise the single-transversal form of tautness uses compactness and connectedness ([[lem-a-taut-foliation-of-a-compact-connected-manifold-is-met-by-a-single-closed-transversal]]); neither implication may be exported without these qualifications.
items.strategy: Recorded as a caveat for the pair: the two notions are kept distinct, Reeblessness is used only where it is proved (the corollary of Novikov's theorem), and tautness is used only in the leaf-by-leaf or single-transversal form proved above. No new mathematics is asserted; the example is cited from Ranz and the qualification from Calegari.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ and let $L$ be a leaf such that the inclusion-induced homomorphism $\pi_1(L)\to\pi_1(M)$ is not injective. Then $F$ admits a vanishing cycle.
items.strategy: Choose a nonzero kernel class in π₁(L), represent it by a C² leaf loop, and span it by a relative C² ambient disk. Put the map into relative characteristic generic position with its prescribed regular leafwise boundary collar, then apply the essential-leafwise-boundary alternative of the finite characteristic-disk supplier. This disk is not used as a leafwise cap.

items.statement: For recurrent caps with simple universal-cover boundaries and a common interior plaque patch, one can choose an increasing sequence of source-disk inclusions whose projected cap maps agree on the included disks, even if the projected caps are immersed.
items.title: Recurrent caps have nested source-disk inclusions
items.strategy: Fix a late cap C_n. Its projected image is compact and is disjoint from the original γ by the avoidance lemma. The compact sets image(C_n) and γ(S¹) are disjoint in a metric ambient manifold, so have positive distance. Uniform convergence γ_t→γ therefore implies that every sufficiently late boundary γ_{t(s_m)} avoids the entire projected image(C_n). Base both lifted caps in the universal cover of B at the same point of their common plaque patch. Their Jordan disk regions Δ_n and Δ_m overlap there, and ∂Δ_m is disjoint from Δ_n because its projection avoids image(C_n). Any path in the connected disk Δ_n from the common interior point to another point cannot exit Δ_m without crossing ∂Δ_m. Hence Δ_n⊂int(Δ_m). The disk parametrizations into Δ_n and Δ_m are diffeomorphisms, so their inverses give a C² embedding h_{n,m}:D²→int D² satisfying C_n=C_m∘h_{n,m} as projected maps. Repeat inductively, selecting one sufficiently late recurrence index at each stage; the choices are countable. This is nesting of source disks in one based universal cover, not a false claim that their ambient projected images are embedded disks. These exact h_{n,m} are the base gluing maps needed by the immersed paired-sweep seam lemma.

items.statement: The primitive Π cap block is an embedded solid torus after attaching its collar to the original leaf, and its foliation is foliated-homeomorphic to the standard Reeb component, with continuous inverse at the boundary.
items.title: The primitive cap block embeds as the standard Reeb component
items.strategy:
Fix a small e and sweep the actual caps over [H(e),e]. Since D_H(e)=D_e∪A_e, identify the whole e-base with its included source disk in the H(e)-base. The quotient X is a solid torus: the disk cylinder is a 3-ball, and identifying two disjoint boundary disks is the attachment of one 1-handle; disk collars explicitly convert this quotient to D²×S¹. The preceding seam charts give a local homeomorphism, piecewise C² and orientation coherent, at every interior point. Its boundary map is an EMBEDDED torus C: the lateral meridian fence is embedded; the unglued base annulus maps to A_e; their interiors are disjoint in the finite collar suspension and they meet only at their two boundary meridians. It is a collar graph over the original torus, with corners removable by local rounding.

Prove global injectivity by preimage counts. For y outside C the finite number n(y) of interior preimages is locally constant: compactness and local injectivity make the fiber finite, finite inverse neighborhoods cover all its points, and the image of their compact complement excludes a small target neighborhood. Every positive cap leaf differs from the original torus, so the whole cap-block image misses that torus. Thus n=0 on the component of M\C containing it. Across C the count changes by exactly1, because its boundary has exactly one preimage and a half-chart; any interior preimages would contribute the same positive count on both sides. Consequently C separates, n=1 on its other component, and C has no interior preimages (one would give positive count on the zero side). There are at most two complement components: both collar sides of connected C are connected, and each complementary component has boundary in C. Hence X maps bijectively onto the closure of the nonzero side. It is a homeomorphism by compactness, and a C² diffeomorphism in the manifold charts after rounding. Attach the product collar between C and the original torus L. This yields a compact solid torus R with boundary exactly L. Since L is a leaf, an ambient leaf cannot cross it; every point in R belongs to one of the cap/annulus leaves, so R is saturated. The previous exhaustion proves that all its interior leaves are planes and their limit set is L.

For the foliated model choose an increasing interval conjugacy ψ with ψ(H(t))=qψ(t), q=1/2. Pick any increasing homeomorphism of [H(e),e] to [qe′,e′], extend over H-iterates by the equation, and put ψ(0)=0. Endpoints match, monotone iterates tend to0, and the inverse construction gives a continuous inverse. In the finite torus suspension collar the map (meridian u, longitude s, transverse t)↦(u,s,ψ(t)) respects the longitude identifications, so it is a foliated homeomorphism to the standard contracting collar. Identify the fundamental cap disks at the two ends with the standard disks, using the exact annulus A_e to make their boundary identifications match. Extend these endpoint disk maps continuously across the compact parameter block: circle boundary maps interpolate by their increasing angle lifts, and disk maps fixing their boundary interpolate by the Alexander radial isotopy; equivalently triangulate the finitely many disk/annulus collars and extend their matching boundary maps cellwise. Choose the endpoint compatibility χ_H(e)∘h=h_std∘χ_e, where h is the included source disk map. Then the product cap maps descend over the paired bases and glue exactly to the collar map. They send every disk/annulus leaf to its standard counterpart, giving a bijective foliated map on the whole interior.

At L the map has the fixed torus base-coordinate map. Any points approaching L eventually lie in an arbitrarily thin compact torus collar, and ψ(t)→0 uniformly in its bounded base coordinates; hence their images approach the corresponding boundary points. Conversely ψ^{-1}(t)→0 gives the same uniform statement for inverse images. Away from L all maps are product/chart homeomorphisms. Thus the global map and inverse are continuous everywhere, including the limiting boundary. This proves the standard Reeb foliated homeomorphism; it asserts no smooth conjugacy of arbitrary contracting germs.

For the disk-map extension, define χ_H(e) on the included disk h(D²) by h_std∘χ_e∘h^{-1}, and define it on its actual complementary annulus by the already specified suspension-collar map. The maps agree on the common meridian. Boundary circle homeomorphisms have increasing angle lifts a(θ+2π)=a(θ)+2π; convex interpolation of two such lifts remains increasing and defines continuous circle maps and inverses. Extend each to the disk radially by re^{iθ}↦re^{ia(θ)}, with0 fixed. After this boundary normalization the endpoint discrepancy k fixes the disk boundary. Its explicit relative-boundary Alexander isotopy is k_r(x)=r k(x/r) for |x|≤r, and k_r(x)=x for r≤|x|≤1; put k_0=id. At |x|=r the formulas agree because k fixes the boundary. The inverse uses the same formula with k^{-1}; the estimate |k_r(x)−x|≤2r proves joint forward and inverse continuity at r=0. This supplies the continuous family of disk maps used across the cap block, with exactly the required paired-base compatibility. The solid-torus differentiable classification uses finite disk collars and the orientable0-handle plus one1-handle charts; it imports no global3-manifold smoothing theorem.

items.statement: For a coherent regular cap family with simple lifted boundaries, an infinite center track, fixed-flow fence, no-hit neighborhood and recurrent nested source disks, the reduced essential initial leaf meets no positive closed transversal.
items.title: An immersed paired cap sweep excludes closed transversals
items.strategy:
The intersections of the original transversal with K are isolated: in a foliation box the transversal has strictly monotone transverse coordinate while each local K branch lies in a plaque. Compactness and finitely many local branches give finitely many intersections, after first a small positive perturbation if necessary to avoid passage through double points of K. Choose disjoint parameter intervals for all intersections other than p and small boxes where each K branch is an embedded arc in one plaque. In box coordinates replace the transversal by a small tangentially shifted arc near its crossing, interpolating to the original arc on end collars. Choose the tangential shift transverse to the one-dimensional branch in the two-dimensional plaque. It misses that branch; the transverse-coordinate derivative stays positive because the shift changes only tangential coordinates. Shrink each box to exclude all other K branches or, at a doublepoint, select a shift avoiding both of the finitely many arcs. The interpolation occurs at transverse levels separated from the branch plaque, so introduces no new intersections. Finite gluing retains C² regularity and positivity. At p keep an interval fixed. The remainder outside a slightly larger p-box is compact and disjoint from K, hence has positive ambient metric distance from K. This last uniform-distance assertion applies only after fixing that box and transversal, not to an arbitrary varying family.

Choose a small box B around the regular initial point p so the initial loop meets B in one embedded arc, with every other boundary parameter outside a larger closed box. Uniform continuity of the short fence keeps those other parameters outside B at all sufficiently small levels. In each plaque met by the boundary, its sole boundary arc is C¹ close to the initial regular arc. A fixed smaller plaque rectangle is therefore split into two connected half-rectangles by this arc, with one uniform tangential and normal size. Lift B to the universal cover of the leaf at that boundary point; the component of the plaque rectangle through the chosen lift maps diffeomorphically to its plaque rectangle. The Jordan boundary has no other boundary points in this lifted rectangle, because all other projected boundary parameters avoid B. Its disk side contains one local half-neighborhood by the boundary collar. Membership in the Jordan interior cannot change along a path in the corresponding half-rectangle without crossing the boundary. Thus the entire chosen half-rectangle lies in the disk. This is inclusion of a local plaque patch, and does not treat the globally projected disk as embedded. Leaf orientation identifies the selected side with the sign of the boundary orientation; on any connected interval with compact cap transport that sign is constant. If global regular cap continuation is unavailable, constancy on the entire interval must be supplied separately.

Suppose a positive closed transversal meets the reduced initial leaf. Finite leaf-path transport and positive perturbation move a crossing to a regular point p of the essential loop γ, away from its finitely many double points. Tangential perturbations in finitely many foliation boxes remove its other intersections with γ, as in the transversal-avoidance lemma. In a fixed-V flowbox near p write coordinates (x,z), with V-orbits vertical and γ an embedded arc in z=0. Replace the local transversal, preserving its positive transverse derivative and its end collars, by τ(r)=(p+r v,r) near r=0, where v is a small vector pointing into the selected local cap half-plaque. For r≠0 sufficiently small its basepoint lies off γ. Since the whole normal fence is made of V-orbits over γ, this local transversal misses the ENTIRE positive fence; the compact remainder of τ has positive distance from γ, so after shrinking the fence it also misses the fence. Hence τ is disjoint from the entire lateral boundary A₀ of every sufficiently late paired sweep.

Fix a late upper cap C_n and its compact projected image, disjoint from γ. Choose the lower recurrent cap C_m sufficiently late that C_n is included in it by the source-disk inclusion h_{n,m}, and that a fixed small neighborhood of p disjoint from image(C_n) contains γ_{t_m} near p. In that box the cap C_m contains the uniform local plaque half-neighborhood from the half-plaque lemma. The local leaf plaque is a graph z=η_m(x) with η_m(p)>0 and tending to0; transversality and small v make r−η_m(p+r v) strictly increasing. It has a small positive zero r_m. At this point τ crosses the C_m plaque on its selected interior side because its tangential displacement r_m v is inward. The crossing lies outside image(C_n), so it belongs to the unglued b-base annulus A₁. Thus τ meets f(A₁), and misses f(A₀) and their boundary seams.

The paired quotient X is an oriented compact 3-manifold with boundary A₀∪A₁: identifying the whole a-base disk to the interior source disk h_{n,m}(D²) of the b-base identifies two boundary disks of the original 3-ball. Local disk collars give manifold charts across the identified bases; its boundary is the remaining b-base annulus and the lateral annulus. The seam lemma strengthens to a local orientation-preserving homeomorphism in the interior: the two half-charts map injectively to opposite sides of their common plaque and agree on that plaque. Other interior charts are regular local diffeomorphisms. Along A₁ the positive transverse direction points inward to X, since this b-base has available cylinder side t<b and the sweep is negatively transverse.

Form the fiber product P={(x,r)∈X×S¹:f(x)=τ(r)}. It is closed in the compact product, hence compact. Interior local homeomorphism charts of f identify P locally with an interval of the oriented transversal; the piecewise C² seam causes no topological defect. Along A₁ transversality gives half-interval charts. There are no points over A₀ or the boundary corners because τ misses their images. Therefore P is a compact oriented 1-manifold with boundary. Its boundary is nonempty by the crossing above. At every boundary point the positive τ direction enters X, so every boundary point has the same boundary sign. This is impossible: a compact oriented 1-manifold has zero total signed boundary. To see this without an imported classification theorem, choose a finite oriented interval-chart cover, subdivide the compact 1-manifold into finitely many short intervals subordinate to it, and cancel paired internal endpoints; each interval contributes one positive and one negative endpoint. Contradiction. Thus the reduced leaf meets no closed positive transversal. This uses multiple-sheet preimages with their multiplicities and never identifies an immersed cap image with an embedded region.

items.statement: Once the original Π supporting leaf L is compact and has no closed transversal, and recurrent cap leaves meet the normal base transversal at t_n↓0, L lies in the ambient boundary of one distinct mutual-positive-accessibility class.
items.title: A recurrent Π-side leaf gives a distinct accessibility boundary
items.strategy:
Use a sufficiently small compact-leaf collar and the nearby compact-leaf graph lemma. Any compact leaf through a positive base parameter t would be a one-sheeted graph over L and would make the transported original essential Π loop essential, contrary to its nullness. Hence every sufficiently near positive Π-side leaf is intrinsically noncompact. The recurrent common-plaque leaf B meets infinitely many positive base parameters t_n↓0, since the cap boundaries on that same leaf include the specified fence basepoints. It is one of these noncompact leaves. By the intrinsic-noncompact-leaf transversal lemma, B meets a positive closed immersed transversal.

Let S be B’s mutual-positive-accessibility class. It is saturated by definition. It is open: the closed transversal gives a strict positive return from B to itself. Finite box transport and small endpoint perturbations of its crossing give strict positive paths from B to every leaf through a small neighborhood of a crossing, and back from each such leaf to B (start and end the loop on opposite sides of the perturbed crossing). These leaves lie in S. Transporting these open crossing neighborhoods along any finite leafwise path gives openness at every point of every leaf in S; for another leaf in S concatenate its strict paths to and from B with the same perturbed return construction. No formal reflexive relation is substituted for a strict positive return.

S is disjoint from L. If L belonged to S, the strict paths L→B and B→L (distinct leaves) would produce a positive closed transversal meeting L after finite plaque-path endpoint alignment and positive corner smoothing. This contradicts the no-transversal conclusion for L. On the other hand the basepoints of the recurrent cap boundaries lie in B⊂S and converge to the original basepoint x∈L, so x∈closure(S). The closure of a saturated set is saturated: in a box its leafwise plaque projection preserves membership of nearby saturation, and a finite chain of such boxes along a leaf carries any accumulation at one point to accumulation at every other point. Hence L⊂closure(S). Since S is open and disjoint from L, L⊂∂_M S. This is an actual distinct mutual-accessibility component boundary, and uses neither an ordinary complement component nor the unsupplied full closure-manifold classification.

items.title: A nonzero limitwise-nullhomotopy class forces a compact boundary leaf
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let F be a C² transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented 3-manifold M. If a leaf L has $\Pi^j_1(L,x)\ne0$ for one side j and base point x, then L is compact and is a boundary leaf of a distinct foliation component in the sense of [[def-foliation-component-by-mutual-positive-transverse-accessibility]]: there is a mutual-accessibility component S with $S\cap L=\varnothing$ and $L\subseteq\partial_M S$. The boundary is the ambient topological boundary.
items.strategy: Normalize the arbitrary nonzero Π representative to a short one-field normal fence. Fixed compact-leafwise separation gives a finite crossing-word rank. At any positive lifted collision cut into two null factors, retain their actual maximal common closed/null interval, and choose an essential lower-endpoint factor; rank decreases, so after ≤N cuts all positive lifts are simple. Canonical based Jordan caps form a Hausdorff proper disk bundle on positive bands; lifted one-field transport gives a coherent regular cap family. The exact finite-clock derivative bound forces an infinite center track. Adjust recurrence to one central plaque; no-hit and common-plaque arguments yield nested SOURCE disks and paired quotients. A closed positive transversal can avoid the whole lateral fence while crossing the inward leafwise annulus; its compact oriented1-manifold pullback gives a one-sign boundary contradiction. Thus reduced leaves have no closed transversals and are compact. Open transversal saturation transfers absence to original L; intrinsic noncompact→transversal makes original L compact. The finite-generator compact-nearby-leaf graph argument prevents any distinct compact reduction leaf at positive parameters, preserving original L. Recurrent Π-side leaf B is noncompact and has a strict positive closed return; its open mutual-accessibility class S is distinct from L, contains basepoints tending to L, and saturation of closure gives L⊂ambient boundary S. The explicitly supplied finite surface, generic-loop, spherical-stability and transversal lemmas discharge those prerequisites; no source citation replaces an argument.

items.title: A nonzero limitwise-nullhomotopy class yields a compact boundary leaf
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$, let $L$ be a leaf, and fix one side $j$. If $\Pi^j_1(L,x)$ is nontrivial for some $x\in L$, then $L$ is compact and lies in the ambient boundary of a distinct foliation component $S$ defined by mutual positive transverse accessibility ([[def-foliation-component-by-mutual-positive-transverse-accessibility]]), with $S\cap L=\varnothing$. In particular, a leaf supporting a vanishing cycle has this property by [[lem-a-vanishing-cycle-determines-a-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class]].
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class-forces-compact-boundary-leaf]] to the stipulated nonzero Π^j class. Its original-leaf compactness and distinct mutual-accessibility boundary are exactly this conclusion. For the particular vanishing-cycle input, [[lem-a-vanishing-cycle-determines-a-nontrivial-limitwise-nullhomotopy-class]] produces that nonzero class on the approached side, and the same implication applies. No complement component or embedded-input weakening is used.

items.title: The compact boundary leaf bounds a Reeb component
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the situation of [[lem-a-simple-vanishing-cycle-produces-a-compact-leaf]], the compact leaf $L_1$ obtained is diffeomorphic to the torus $T^2$, and there is a Reeb component $R\subseteq M$ with $\partial R=L_1$: $R$ is a compact saturated submanifold diffeomorphic to $D^2\times S^1$ with boundary leaf $L_1$, every interior leaf of $R$ is a plane, and $(R,F|_R)$ is foliated-homeomorphic to the standard Reeb component ([[def-reeb-component-in-a-cooriented-three-manifold-foliation]]). Moreover, on the side $j$ of the nonzero $\Pi^j_1$ class (the side approached by the vanishing-cycle family when one is given), $L_1$ is the limit set of every sufficiently nearby displaced leaf: for a corresponding one-sided normal fence based at the supporting leaf, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that the leaf $A_t$ through its displaced base point has limit set exactly $L_1$ for $0<t<\varepsilon$.
items.strategy: The original compact leaf has no closed transversal. Its strict positive accessible region has finite compact inward boundary; finite plane-bundle Euler boundary evaluation and finite oriented-surface normal forms identify original L as a torus. Extract a primitive embedded Π meridian on L: increasing finite-order holonomy is identity and torsion-free nearby surface groups turn the displaced root null. The full primitive fixed-flow fence is embedded, so its positive circles bound actual embedded Jordan disks. A complementary longitude has no small fixed point (otherwise the compact graph lemma contradicts meridian nullness); choose its inverse to obtain a contraction H. Finite collar suspension gives embedded leafwise longitude annuli and D_H(t)=D_t∪A_t; iterates exhaust whole nearby leaves as planes with limit set exactly original L. The fundamental cap sweep paired quotient has embedded boundary torus C; proper local inverse preimage counts, zero on the original-leaf side and jumping1 across C, prove the entire quotient is globally embedded as a solid torus. Attach its compact collar to original L. Saturation follows because boundary L is a leaf and all block/collar points are in the exhausting plane leaves. Interval contraction conjugacy, compatible disk/annulus extension and uniform forward/inverse collar control produce the global foliated homeomorphism to standard Reeb. The finite surface/index/spherical-stability and explicit disk-extension lemmas provide the listed local prerequisites; no source sentence substitutes for these constructions.

items.title: Novikov's Reeb component theorem
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$. If either (a) some leaf $L$ of $F$ has non-injective inclusion-induced homomorphism $\pi_1(L)\to\pi_1(M)$, or (b) some closed transversal $\gamma:S^1\to M$ is null-homotopic in $M$, then $F$ contains a Reeb component ([[def-reeb-component-in-a-cooriented-three-manifold-foliation]]). Equivalently, a Reebless $C^2$ transversely oriented foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold has all leaves $\pi_1$-injective and all closed transversals essential (cor-reebless-leaves-are-pi-one-injective-under-novikov-hypotheses).
items.strategy: In branch(a), [[lem-a-compressible-leaf-yields-a-vanishing-cycle]] supplies a vanishing cycle. In branch(b), [[lem-a-nullhomotopic-closed-transversal-yields-a-vanishing-cycle]] supplies one. In either branch apply [[lem-a-simple-vanishing-cycle-produces-a-compact-leaf]], then [[lem-the-compact-leaf-produced-by-a-vanishing-cycle-bounds-a-reeb-component]]. The latter supplies a compact saturated solid torus whose foliation is foliated-homeomorphic to the standard Reeb model, so it satisfies the stated Reeb-component definition. Both alternatives are proved; its extra Π-side limit-set clause is unnecessary for this existence conclusion.

items.title: Reebless leaves are pi-one-injective and transverse loops are essential
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ containing no Reeb component. Then: (i) for every leaf $L$ of $F$ the inclusion-induced homomorphism $\pi_1(L)\to\pi_1(M)$ is injective; and (ii) every closed transversal to $F$ represents a nontrivial class in $\pi_1(M)$.
items.strategy: If a leaf inclusion map were noninjective, alternative(a) of [[thm-novikov-reeb-component-theorem]] would produce a Reeb component, contradicting Reeblessness. Thus all leaf maps are injective. If any closed transversal were null-homotopic, alternative(b) would give the same contradiction. Hence every closed transversal represents a nontrivial ambient class. This proves both asserted conclusions under the same C²/coorientation/closedness/ACω hypotheses.

items.title: Novikov's conclusions do not extend to higher dimensions or noncompact manifolds
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Novikov's theorem is deliberately three-dimensional and codimension one. In higher dimensions the analogue fails even for codimension-one strongly symplectic foliations: Venugopalan constructs a closed $5$-manifold with a codimension-one foliation whose leaves have non-injective inclusion in the fundamental group of the ambient manifold and which admits a closed transversal that is null-homotopic in the ambient manifold, with no Reeb-type component; so neither hypothesis of [[thm-novikov-reeb-component-theorem]] forces a Reeb component once the dimension exceeds three. The compactness hypothesis also cannot be dropped: the crossing example of the companion page removes a point from a closed three-manifold foliated by dense cylinders and produces a noncompact $3$-manifold with a Reebless foliation and a leaf whose inclusion is not $\pi_1$-injective, so the conclusion of [[cor-reebless-leaves-are-pi-one-injective-under-novikov-hypotheses]] fails without compactness (the leaf escapes through the puncture). Both restrictions are part of the statement and are not artefacts of the proof.
items.strategy: Recorded as a scope caveat with its sources. No new mathematics is asserted: the higher-dimensional counterexample is cited from Venugopalan (as reported in Ranz's introduction), and the noncompact phenomenon is the phenomenon exhibited on the companion examples page. Nothing on this page is applied outside codimension one and dimension three without an explicit hypothesis.

items.title: A fibration over the circle has zero Godbillon-Vey class
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:M\to S^1$ be a smooth fibre bundle with connected fibre and let $F$ be the foliation of $M$ by the fibres of $q$. Then $F$ is a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation defined by the closed nowhere-vanishing $1$-form $\omega=q^{*}d\theta$, where $d\theta$ is the standard volume form on $S^1$, and consequently $\mathrm{GV}(F)=0$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. In particular the fibre foliation of the mapping torus of a diffeomorphism of a closed surface has zero Godbillon-Vey class.
items.strategy: The fibres of a submersion are the leaves of the kernel foliation of $q^{*}d\theta$, and $q^{*}d\theta$ is closed and nowhere vanishing because $q$ is a submersion and $d\theta$ is a volume form; hence $F$ is defined by a closed form and [[cor-a-codimension-one-foliation-defined-by-a-closed-one-form-has-zero-godbillon-vey-class]] gives $\mathrm{GV}(F)=0$. The mapping-torus case is the explicit construction of [[prop-mapping-torus-foliations-realize-global-reeb-stable-examples]], where the base projection is the bundle map. The example verifies the basic vanishing test of the page against the standard positive model of a compact-leaf foliation.

items.title: Explicit Godbillon-Vey rescaling calculation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On $M=\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,z)$ let $\varphi=ze^{x^2/2}$, so that $\omega:=e^{-x^2/2}\,d\varphi=dz+xz\,dx$ is a nowhere-vanishing defining form and $F=\ker\omega$ is the regular codimension-one foliation by the surfaces $z=ce^{-x^2/2}$, $c\in\mathbb R$. The $1$-form $\eta=(xyz-x)\,dx+y\,dz$ satisfies $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, and $d\eta=-xz\,dx\wedge dy-xy\,dx\wedge dz+dy\wedge dz\neq0$ with $\eta\wedge d\eta=-x\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, nonzero where $x\neq0$. For the rescaled defining form $\omega'=e^{y}\omega$, the form $\eta'=\eta+dy$ satisfies $d\omega'=\eta'\wedge\omega'$, $d\eta'=d\eta$, and $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=\eta\wedge d\eta+dy\wedge d\eta=\eta\wedge d\eta+d(y\,d\eta)=(xy-x)\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$; the difference is the exact form $d(y\,d\eta)$, the explicit instance of [[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-invariant-under-rescaling-the-defining-form]] with $f=y$.
items.strategy: The function $\varphi=ze^{x^2/2}$ has $d\varphi=e^{x^2/2}\omega$ nowhere zero, so $\varphi$ is a submersion and $F=\ker\omega=\ker d\varphi$ is integrable with the stated level surfaces as leaves by [[cor-kernel-of-a-constant-rank-submersion-is-integrable]], and is a regular codimension-one foliation by [[thm-regular-foliations-and-integrable-distributions-correspond]]. The identities $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, $d\eta=-xz\,dx\wedge dy-xy\,dx\wedge dz+dy\wedge dz$ and $\eta\wedge d\eta=-x\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$ are direct exterior-derivative computations: $d\omega=x\,dz\wedge dx$ and $\eta\wedge\omega=(xyz-x)\,dx\wedge dz+xyz\,dz\wedge dx=-x\,dx\wedge dz$. For $\omega'=e^{y}\omega$ one has $d\omega'=e^{y}(dy\wedge\omega+d\omega)=e^{y}(dy+\eta)\wedge\omega=(\eta+dy)\wedge\omega'$, so $\eta'=\eta+dy$ is admissible and $d\eta'=d\eta$; then $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=\eta\wedge d\eta+dy\wedge d\eta$ and $dy\wedge d\eta=xy\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz=d(y\,d\eta)$ is exact, which is the explicit instance of [[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-invariant-under-rescaling-the-defining-form]]. Both Godbillon-Vey forms therefore define the same class in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$ ([[def-de-rham-cohomology]]).

items.title: The Reeb foliation of the three-sphere is not taut
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The Reeb foliation $F_{\mathrm{Reeb}}$ of $S^3$, obtained by gluing two Reeb solid tori along their boundary tori ([[prop-gluing-two-reeb-components-gives-a-foliation-of-s-three]]), contains two Reeb components meeting along the single compact leaf, the Heegaard torus $T^2$. Consequently $F_{\mathrm{Reeb}}$ is not taut: the torus leaf is the boundary leaf of both Reeb components, and no closed transversal meets it. Every other leaf is a plane accumulating on the torus.
items.strategy: The gluing proposition supplies the foliation and the identification of the two solid tori as Reeb components with common boundary leaf the Heegaard torus; the definition of Reeb component is satisfied with the foliated homeomorphism supplied by the model. By [[lem-a-reeb-component-obstructs-tautness]] a foliation containing a Reeb component is not taut, and the accessible manifold of the torus leaf is not all of $S^3$: transverse curves crossing the torus into either solid torus are trapped by the accumulating plane leaves. This is Ranz's statement that a foliated manifold containing a Reeb component is not taut, realised in the standard example; it verifies the obstruction and supplies the negative model dual to the fibre-foliation example.

items.title: A fibre foliation of a mapping torus is taut
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $L$ be a closed connected smooth manifold and $f:L\to L$ a diffeomorphism, with mapping torus $M_f=(L\times\mathbb R)/\mathbb Z$, where $k\cdot(x,t)=(f^k(x),t+k)$, and fibre foliation $F_f$ ([[prop-mapping-torus-foliations-realize-global-reeb-stable-examples]]). Every leaf is compact and diffeomorphic to $L$. There is a smooth path $a:[0,1]\to L$, constant near its endpoints, with $a(1)=f(a(0))$, and its graph $t\mapsto[a(t),t]$ descends to a smooth embedded closed transversal meeting every fibre exactly once. Consequently $F_f$ is taut and a single closed transversal meets all its leaves.
items.strategy: A connected smooth manifold is path connected; join a chosen $x_0$ to $f(x_0)$ by a finite smooth chartwise path, smooth its finitely many corners and reparametrize it to be constant near $0$ and $1$. Extend by $a(t+k)=f^k(a(t))$. Stationary ends make the extension smooth across every integer and $[a(t),t]$ periodic under the diagonal mapping-torus action. The induced graph over $S^1$ is embedded because its composition with the base projection is the identity; its derivative has base component $1$, so it is transverse to the fibre foliation. It meets every fibre once, proving the leaf-by-leaf condition of [[def-taut-codimension-one-foliation]] directly. No fixed point of $f$ is assumed.

items.title: A noncompact foliation violating Novikov's compactness conclusions
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N_0=T^2\times S^1$ and let $F_0$ be the codimension-one foliation defined by the closed $1$-form $\omega=dy-\lambda\,dx$ with $\lambda$ irrational, where $(x,y)$ are coordinates on the first torus factor: the leaves are the cylinders $\{y-\lambda x=c\}\times S^1$, dense and noncompact, and $F_0$ is Reebless. Remove a point $p\in N_0$ and set $M=N_0\setminus\{p\}$, $F=F_0|_M$. Then $M$ is a noncompact $3$-manifold, $F$ is a codimension-one Reebless foliation of $M$, and the leaf $L$ through $p$ becomes $L\setminus\{p\}$, whose fundamental group is free of rank two; a small loop in $L\setminus\{p\}$ around the puncture bounds a disk in $M$ (inside a coordinate ball from which $p$ is removed, the loop bounds a disk avoiding $p$), so $\pi_1(L\setminus\{p\})\to\pi_1(M)$ is not injective. Thus the conclusion of [[cor-reebless-leaves-are-pi-one-injective-under-novikov-hypotheses]] fails without compactness, and the hypotheses of [[thm-novikov-reeb-component-theorem]] do not force a Reeb component in the noncompact case: the leaf escapes at the puncture.
items.strategy: The form $\omega=dy-\lambda dx$ is closed and nowhere vanishing, so its kernel is integrable by [[prop-closed-constant-rank-one-forms-define-integrable-hyperplane-fields]] and its level sets are the cylinders $y-\lambda x=c$ times $S^1$; since $\lambda$ is irrational these are noncompact and dense, so no compact leaf and no Reeb component exists. Removing a point does not create a Reeb component (a Reeb component of the restricted foliation would be a compact foliated solid torus in $M$ and hence in $N_0$). The leaf through $p$ is the connected surface $L\setminus\{p\}$; retracting $L$ to the puncture's complement realises it as a once-punctured annulus, with free fundamental group of rank two, while the small loop around $p$ bounds the complement of a small disk in the coordinate ball, so it is null-homotopic in $M$. Hence inclusion is not injective, exhibiting the failure of the compactness conclusion of the theorem. The construction is the standard escape-at-infinity phenomenon; only the standing countable choice is used.
